text:
#PrinceOnThisDay

On 17 October 2009, subscribers to Prince’s https://t.co/tyaTeC8yjZ membership site received three exclusive MP3 downloads: live acoustic versions of “Feel Better, Feel Good, Feel Wonderful” and a “Mountains” / “Shake Your Body (Down to the Ground)” medley (both recorded in Paris on 12 October), plus a Paisley Park rehearsal of “Y U Wanna Treat Me So Bad?” (recorded 21 September). 

These were high-quality 320 kbps files tied to Prince’s 2009 independent era—the site launched with the Lotusflow3r / MPLSound / Elixer triple set and offered occasional extras to members. The Paris tracks came from a short, intimate acoustic set at RTL’s Le Grand Studio (Rue Bayard) for the Antony Martin show, the day after Prince’s two sold-out Grand Palais concerts and hours before a La Cigale aftershow. Joining him were Shelby J., Liv Warfield, and Elisa Dease on vocals plus French harmonica player Frédéric Yonnet. The full set also included “North Carolina” (Shelby J. lead); accounts describe roughly ten minutes of stripped-down intensity with strong vocal harmonies, more folk-tinged intimacy than full-band funk. 

“Feel Better, Feel Good, Feel Wonderful” (live, ~2:51):
The Lotusflow3r studio version is a buoyant, horn-laced funk track with a mantra-like positive chorus. This acoustic take shifts the focus to the title phrase and vocal blend. With the three singers and Yonnet’s harmonica, it emphasizes warmth and group harmony over the original’s groove and guitar. It captures the “feel better, feel good, feel wonderful” sentiment in a quieter, more communal setting—effective as a live counterpart and a rare official acoustic document from the era. 

“Mountains” / “Shake Your Body (Down to the Ground)” (live medley, ~4:17)
A seamless pairing of the Parade-era “Mountains” into the Jacksons’ 1978 disco classic. Elisa Dease takes lead on the Jacksons section. Released just months after Michael Jackson’s death, it is one of the first official Prince-related releases of a Jackson track (no studio Prince cover is known). The acoustic arrangement and harmonica keep it intimate while still dance-oriented; it highlights the band’s versatility and Prince’s habit of spotlighting his singers. Later tours featured full-band versions of the medley. 

“Y U Wanna Treat Me So Bad?” (rehearsal, ~3:44):
A Paisley Park rehearsal from 21 September 2009 with C.C. Dunham (drums), Joshua Dunham (bass), Morris Hayes (keys), and Prince on guitar and lower-register vocals. It revisits the early rock-leaning track from the 1979 Prince album, fades into a tease of “Take Me With U,” and shows the band tightening material ahead of European dates. The lower octave and rehearsal energy differ from the classic falsetto-driven studio cut; it was shared earlier via Dr. Funkenberry before (or around) the site availability. 

Overall, these drops rewarded Lotusflow3r members with rare official soundboard material—intimate Paris acoustics that contrast the big Grand Palais shows, plus a tight rehearsal of a deep cut. They exemplify Prince’s 2009 approach of controlled, high-quality online exclusives rather than wide commercial singles. The site closed in March 2010; these files were never widely reissued.

text:
The Guardian Angels' Services to Us.
. 
HOW much we owe to our Guardian  Angels! God in His infinite mercy! and condescension makes use of their agency to bestow upon the weak and needy children of men an abundance of material and spiritual blessings. The Angels are the first-born "children" of the Heavenly Father and as such are our elder "brothers," forming with us but one great family of God. Just as parents sometimes entrust the younger members of the family to the care of their elder brothers and sisters, so our Heavenly Father commits us to the care of the holy Angels. But the love of the Angels for their charges upon earth far exceeds in strength and tenderness the love of a brother or sister, or even that of parents.
If we but knew all the favors which we continually receive from the holy Angels, our hearts would indeed be harder than stone not to be sensibly affected thereby. It would be necessary to reckon up all the evils which can befall us-----whether in mind or body, in our spiritual or temporal goods, in regard to our private or public interests, by wars, pestilences or famines-----in order to specify all the various kinds of assistance we receive from the Angels. Their constant thought and unremitting care is to preserve us from sin, or to deliver us from it when we have fallen. They obtain powerful graces for us from the mercy of God, moderate our passions, remove hindrances to our use of grace and assist us to triumph over the evil one in temptations. They discover to us our faults and imperfections and move us to sincere contrition.
.
Father Faber touchingly describes this solicitude of our Guardian Angels: "Ever at our side is being lived a golden life. A princely Spirit is there who sees God and enjoys the bewildering splendors of His Face, even there where he is, nearer than the limits of our outstretched arms. An unseen warfare is waging round our steps, but that beautiful Spirit lets not so much as the sound of it vex our ears. He fights for us and asks no thanks, but hides his silent victories, and continues to gaze upon God. His tenderness for us is above all words. His office will last beyond the grave, until at length it merges into a still sweeter tie of something like heavenly equality, when on the morning of the resurrection we pledge each other, in those first moments, to an endless blessed love. Till then we shall never know from how many dangers he has delivered us, nor how much of our salvation is actually due to him. Meanwhile he merits nothing by the solicitudes of his office. He is beyond the power of meriting, for he has attained the sight of God. His work is a work of love because his sweet presence at our side he knows to be a part of God's eternal creative love towards our particular soul."
"Wherever we go," writes Cardinal O'Connell in his beautiful pastoral on the holy Angels, "this Angelic partnership is never interrupted. Heavenly Spirits shield us from bodily danger and minister to us in our temporal needs . . . Intent upon the salvation of our souls, they instruct us, they protect us, they plead for us with God. They ward off temptations, overcome obstacles-----physical as well as spiritual-----and pointing out the path of virtue, they guide us lest we go astray. To our prayers they unite theirs; they inspire holy thoughts or whisper helpful inspirations: at times, too, they inflict upon us healing and salutary chastisements. To every want of the soul through life they minister, that they may assist it to arrive safely at its journey's end. All this they do for us, if we but let them; every help that they can give us is ours, if we but welcome them and gratefully co-operate with them.
.
"Many are the motives which prompt such constant devotion to our interests. These celestial patrons, we know, are close to the merciful Heart of the Redeemer; they understand, therefore, His untiring concern for our welfare, and from that inexhaustible Fountain of love they imbibe the tenderest affection in our regard. They know, too, that we, their relatives-----not by the flesh but through the spirit element in our nature-----are destined to share their glory, to be their fellow-citizens in Heaven, and one day to enter into their unending companionship. In the unselfishness of their love, they are anxious for the period of our probation to close triumphantly.
"However, what especially enhances the intensity of their affection is the fact that they have a Divine commission to watch over us and to be for us here upon earth the instruments of God's mercies. This it is that urges them to sweep down from their golden skies, to flash swiftly and joyously through the dim air of this lower world, that they may assure us of their love and be at hand in all fear and trouble.
.
"And with what admirable solicitude and unceasing watchfulness do these protecting Angels fulfill their Divine commission with regard to us! At every moment, though unseen, they are by our side. They never forsake us from the first breath we draw until we have entered into the possession of our eternal destiny. They hover about the babe slumbering in its crib; they guide the timid and untried steps with which childhood and youth enter upon life, at first so strange and at all times so full of peril. They hold out a helping hand to strong and rugged manhood, seasoned by struggles with the forces of evil, and bearing, perhaps, the scars which the wounds of sins have made. And when the light of life is transformed into the darkness and gloom of age, with its dreams unrealized and its hopes cherished in vain, Guardian Angels are near to support the bent form and tottering steps, and to banish the shadows of loneliness and sorrow."
.
The good offices which the holy Guardian Angels perform in our behalf may be briefly summed up as follows:
.
1. They preserve us from many unknown dangers to soul and body. 
2. They defend us against the temptations of the evil spirits. 
3. They inspire us with holy thoughts and prompt us to deeds of virtue in the Divine service. 
4. They warn us of spiritual dangers and admonish us when we have sinned. 
5. They unite with us in prayer and offer our prayers to God. 
6. They defend us at the hour of death against the last attacks of our spiritual foes. 
7. They console the souls languishing in Purgatory and conduct them to Heaven when their faults have been fully expiated.
.
 1. They Protect Us in Perils.
.
Innumerable instances of the protection of the Angels in physical dangers may be cited from Holy Scripture, from the lives of the Saints and from the daily experience of ordinary persons. Among those mentioned in the Scriptures are the rescue of Lot and his family from the city of Sodom, the protection of the three Hebrew youths in the fiery furnace of Babylon, the assistance rendered to Judas the Machabee and his army, and the rescue of St. Peter in prison.
.
In the life of St. Gregory of Tours it is related that while he was still a boy his father became dangerously ill. The devoted son prayed earnestly for his good father. That night his Guardian Angel appeared to him in sleep, saying: "Arise, write the Name of Jesus on a small wooden chip and lay it on your father's pillow." In the morning Gregory related the vision to his mother, who bade him do as he had been told. He obeyed, and the father immediately regained his health. Two years later, the father again became ill. Gregory once more had recourse to prayer, and again his Guardian Angel appeared to him in sleep, instructing him to use the liver of a fish, as had been done in the case of Tobias. This admonition was followed and the father was cured a second time.
.
A striking incident of recent occurrence in one of our Southern states was the rescue of a young boy from drowning. On a bright, sunny day in May, Sister M. took her pupils to the woods to pick berries. After the merry group had spent a happy day and had filled all their baskets with berries, they started for home. On their homeward journey, it was necessary to cross a small stream, and several of the older boys asked permission to wade across rather than to cross on the bridge. As the stream had every appearance of being shallow, Sister M. readily granted the permission.
One of the most sturdy boys went ahead, but what was the surprise and horror of all when he suddenly disappeared from sight beneath the water! He had stepped into a deep hole, and as he was unable to swim, he floundered helplessly about, unable to regain his footing. Sister M. ordered all the other boys back to the bank of the stream, and with a fervent invocation to her Guardian Angel-----whose help she had often experienced-----she herself was preparing to go to the rescue of the boy, who had just gone down for the second time.
.
Suddenly, as if by magic, two stalwart youths stepped out of an automobile, which had come up unnoticed, and went hurriedly to the bank. One of them stood beside Sister, while the other, without a word, descended into the water up to his head, took the boy in his arms and carried him safely back to his teacher. Sister thanked the young man most cordially and inquired his name. He merely smiled and said:
.
"What does it matter-----the boy is safe." Astonishing to relate, his clothes seemed perfectly dry when he and his companion returned to the car. Then they left so quickly that no trace could be seen of them on the road. Sister M. breathed a prayer of thanksgiving to her good Guardian Angel, for she was firmly convinced that it was he who had once again come to her assistance.
Though the holy Angels are most solicitous for our bodily welfare, yet still greater is their solicitude for the welfare of immortal souls. It is especially when the virtue of holy purity is assailed that the Guardian Angels lend their powerful protection to their protégés, as is witnessed in the lives of St. Agnes, St. Agatha, St. Cecilia, St. Lucy, St. Theophila and other Saints.
.
A touching story of a Guardian Angel's protection of an innocent youth is related by the renowned Jesuit, Father Coret. One day in 1638, a young nobleman appeared at the monastery at noon and asked to see a certain priest. The priest came and, immediately upon seeing the stranger, received the impression that this was an Angel. The heavenly appearance, the majestic bearing and the Angelic demeanor of the young man were most striking. His countenance was fair, his eyes exceedingly kind, his hair blond, his features mild and delicate. The noble visitor apologized for coming at so inconvenient a time, but added, "The zeal with which you labor for the honor of God and the salvation of youth urges me to leave nothing undone when the innocence and perhaps the eternal salvation of one of your pupils is in peril. You are acquainted with the youth, N.?" The young man in question was a nobleman, about sixteen years of age, very handsome, possessed of great virtue and beloved by all. "Oh, how you would love him if you knew him as I do!" continued the stranger. "He is an Angel, but alas, into what danger of temptation will he be led today! He has been invited to a banquet. If he goes, it will be at the price of his innocence; he will suffer an irreparable loss!"
.
Naturally, the priest was greatly surprised at his statement. He inquired of the stranger who he was and how he had learned of the snares which had been laid for the youth, but he received no other answer than that the youth was as pure as an Angel, very dear to God, and that his Guardian Angel was most solicitous to preserve his innocence. Then the stranger added, "Often I am in the midst of those who would lead him astray. I come in the name of God and conjure you to prevent so great an evil. Be convinced that as the demons exert an their power to corrupt youth, the Guardian Angels likewise do their utmost to protect them."
.
The stranger took his leave, and the priest hastened to inform the mother and the son of what had happened. He then made a search for his distinguished visitor, but he was never seen again, and the priest never doubted that this had been the youth's Guardian Angel.
.
2. They Defend Us against the Demons.
.
In the hour of temptation, when the enemies from Hell break in upon us, the holy Angels intervene in our behalf and help us to conquer the craftiness of the enemy. They strengthen us in the fight, warn us against the suggestions of the tempter, disclose to us his snares and make us fear evil. The fallen angels, retaining the keen and penetrating knowledge proper to their spirit nature, wage fierce and constant battles against those creatures whom God had commanded them to serve. In their morbid despair and jealousy, with a strength surpassing the utmost might of man, they aim at our destruction. "Our wrestling," says St. Paul, "is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities and the powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in the high places." [Eph. 6: 12]. But the paternal care of God shields us from their malevolent attacks by surrounding us with the protection of our good Angels. "God," says St. Augustine, "has subjected the bad Angels to the good; they cannot do as much harm as they wish, but only as much as they are permitted for our trial and punishment."
.
3. They Inspire Holy Thoughts.
.
"Your holy Angel is tender, gentle and mild," says the devout spiritual writer, Hermas. "When he takes possession of your heart, he speaks of justice, modesty and benignity, of true love and piety. When such things make themselves felt in your heart, know that your holy Angel is with you."
.
It is peculiar to the good Angels to enlighten and instruct the soul of man, to inspire it with strength and fortitude and also, by spiritual consolations, by gentle persuasions, by calmness and refreshing peace, to lighten the fulfillment of every duty and to remove all hindrances to advancement in virtue. "Return to thy mistress, and humble thyself under her hand" [Gen. 16: 9], said an Angel to Agar, the handmaid of Abraham and Sara, thus reminding her of her duty. St. Raphael taught the young Tobias how he should enter the married state in the holy fear of God and how, together with his parents, he should adore and praise God. [Cf. Tob. 11-12]. Likewise, it was an Angel who exhorted the Roman centurion Cornelius to seek out St. Peter in order to be instructed by him in the True Faith. [Cf. Acts 10: 30].
.
4. They Warn and Admonish Us.
.
Before the city of Jerusalem was captured by the Romans, voices were heard above the Temple saying, "Let us withdraw from hence!" Similarly, our holy Guardian Angel often urges us to leave those places, those companionships, those conversations, books and pastimes where danger threatens our soul and where, because of his Angelic purity and delicacy, he cannot bear us company. His voice cries out to us in various ways-----through the counsel of a friend, through the reading of a good book, through the voice of conscience, etc. How often, how lovingly, how mildly he instructs, warns, entreats and invites us! He is most anxious to be our advocate at the throne of God, but if we do not heed his voice he will be compelled to be our accuser, for he can only fulfill his sublime task if we cooperate with him with ready willingness. If we harden our heart and refuse to heed his admonitions, he will one day be compelled to reveal our sins before all the world.
Disobedience on our part would therefore be not only the basest ingratitude, but the greatest folly as well, for it is only for our own eternal welfare that our Angel thus warns us.
.
Our Guardian Angel is likewise our loving admonitor. To reprove is an act very proper to love, for since love cherishes an inmost desire for the good of the beloved and shows itself also in deed, so it seeks to avert evil from the one beloved. The administering of reproofs is a means toward this end, and this the Angel accomplishes by inflicting the sting of remorse of conscience. The moment we have committed sin, our holy Angel withdraws his consolations and pierces our soul with pain. He strives to awaken in our heart vehement qualms of conscience and to move us to true contrition and penance. How great are our obligations toward this true friend who thus warns us of evil, chastises us and fills us with anxiety when we have done wrong!
.
5. They Pray with Us and for Us.
.
Holy Scripture clearly teaches that the Angels pray in our behalf. The Prophet Zacharias, speaking of the supplicating Angels who were watching over Jerusalem, says, "The angel of the Lord answered, and said: 'O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and the cities of Juda?' " [Zach. 1: 12]. And the Archangel Raphael said to Tobias, "When thou didst pray with tears . . . I offered thy prayer to the Lord." [Tob. 12: 12]. St. Augustine says: "The Angels pray for us, not as if God did not know our needs, but the sooner to obtain for us the gift of His mercy and to secure for us the blessings of His grace."
.
On one occasion, while assisting at Holy Mass with special fervor, St. Gertrude was rapt in ecstasy. In this state she saw her Guardian Angel bearing her prayers to the throne of the Divine Majesty, presenting them to the three Divine Persons and imploring them to hear her petitions. The prayer of the Guardian Angel was accepted and Gertrude was blessed by each Person of the Godhead.
St. Bernard frequently admonished his disciples to conduct themselves in an edifying manner in the performance of their devotional exercises, lest their Guardian Angels, who took part in them, should withdraw. "How happy you would be," he exclaimed, "if you could see how they hasten to join those who sing the Psalms and with what reverential bearing they remain among them! They assist those who pray and meditate. With great solicitude they go back and forth between God and us, bearing our sighs to the throne of God. Let us therefore strive earnestly to make their joy complete."
.
It is related that St. Gregory of Tours and others who slept at the time of prayer received a blow from their Guardian Angel. The histories of religious orders recount many instances of holy souls being awakened by their Angels for prayer in the morning and being punished by them for small faults, such as not rising immediately or not giving themselves to meditation with sufficient fervor.

text:
REVIEW: Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4

CAMPAIGN: Modern Warfare 4 has the best COD campaign since MW2019. It is an excellent story that stands as some of the franchise's best ever work. After the misses of BO7/MW3, It felt like this franchise may never reach the heights it did in the early years with its storytelling, but I am happy to report that MW4's campaign is a stellar conclusion to the rebooted Modern Warfare saga.

STORY

Modern Warfare 4 takes place three years after the ending of MW3, with Captain Price going rogue after taking out Shepard. The campaign follows Price as he "crosses the line" and faces off against his very own Task Force 141 in order to achieve his goal of taking out the Archer, played by Mads Mikkelsen. 

The other half of the plot centers around a North Korean invasion of South Korea, playing as Private Park as the invasion unfolds, alongside various other perspectives around this conflict.

I absolutely loved MW4's story. It is an enthralling, breakneck-paced tale. It brings together all my favourite characters with Price/Ghost/Gaz and pits them against each other in some of this franchise's best-written moments. Any fears I had of the plot potentially cheapening out and quickly resolving this long-hyped conflict are entirely gone. The Archer is easily the best villain that COD has had in many years, he has clear motivations, an actual background, a reason to hate our characters, and is played incredibly by the always awesome Mads Mikkelsen. 

Captain Price, Ghost, and Gaz have always been beloved for good reason, and MW4 manages to give these characters their most emotional story so far. There's a deep sense of loss in these characters since they lost Soap in MW3, Price acts more like the Punisher, and in general, it feels like this family has been entirely broken by the events of the trilogy. In comparison to the old original MW trilogy, this MW4 campaign almost feels like an extended epilogue. Where Soap's death in the original MW3 was near the ending, the characters here get a full game to grapple with the reality of what has happened.

The second half of the campaign, the one focused on the Korean conflict, is less plot-heavy and instead far more focused on the conflict itself. It very much is focused on spectacle and is where those huge battle moments that COD campaigns are known for happen. It does have its moments, however, and I found the cast of marines to be lovable by the end.

MW4's biggest upgrade over the last few COD campaigns is that it actually feels consequential— none of that "we are too scared to kill any major character because we wanna bring them back in the post-launch seasons!" issue that’s been plaguing the storytelling for years now. Instead, things feel truly final here. Important deaths absolutely do happen, and it very much feels like the writers do not hold back one bit on making sure all arcs are properly paid off here in the campaign alone. Without relying on the post-launch cutscenes to actually wrap it up. 

Overall, this is easily COD's strongest story in years. It avoids all the pitfalls of the duds that were MW3/BO7, it avoids BO6's issue of having a weak villain and failing to wrap up its own story in the campaign, overall resulting in MW4's campaign being easily the best COD campaign since MW2019 and maybe even surpassing that one. Infinity Ward have truly cooked writing-wise here.

GAMEPLAY

Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4's campaign plays like a COD campaign, so there isn't anything groundbreaking in its core gameplay design. What it does, however, offer is a whole load of unique gameplay scenarios. One mission you quite literally are thrown into a John Wick-style nightclub with just a pistol to take on an army of thugs. Another mission has you fighting through trench warfare. The levels in general are quite open and do avoid that feeling of being too linear that older COD games had. 

They did add a melee combat in this game, complete with a parry system. It's pretty fun and a nice change of pace from the usual COD gameplay. The finishers especially are animated very well and give the fights a great feel.

There's one mission that tries the open-world style once again, that was attempted in MW3/BO6/BO7 and honestly, this ended up being my least favorite part of the game. While the rest of the campaign is at breakneck speed, this one mission really does slow things down, and it’s the one 20-minute stretch of game that I felt MW4 lets up and gets far too slow for my own taste. I would prefer if this franchise stops experimenting with open-world missions. It feels like they always let down what most of us play COD campaigns for, which is intricately crafted setpieces.

And speaking of those setpieces, they are in huge abundance in MW4. After how disappointing and empty MW3 felt, MW4 has constant setpieces, car chases, massive destruction sequences, and large battles. Infinity Ward has done a fantastic job making this campaign feel as big as it does. It has a couple of moments of silliness, but it’s COD so that’s expected. I'd honestly love to be more specific on which setpieces stood out to me, but I want to avoid spoilers. All I will say is that everything involving Price was my favorite.

Overall, the gameplay is about what you expect from COD but the major setpieces do make this campaign stand out in a major way. No level is as memorable as the Zombies level from BO6, but pretty much all levels are fun to get through and consistently offer big setpieces.

GRAPHICS

COD has honestly looked the same for a while since MW2019. MW4 is a very beautiful game, and it is quite a step up from BO7 and MW3 but it’s not radically better than, say, MW2019. The main improvement is in-game facial animations, which are getting to a point where they rival the CGI cutscenes. Explosion effects look way better as well, but overall, COD has looked fantastic for quite a long while. So there isn't anything too major here to write home about.

MW4 performed perfectly on my PS5 Pro. It runs at a locked 60FPS, with zero noticeable drops. It also looks absolutely gorgeous and high-res. COD games have been well optimized for a long while, so no real surprise here.

FINAL VERDICT

Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4's campaign is genuinely fantastic. It is the best COD campaign since MW2019. It avoids the many pitfalls of the last few COD campaigns by having well-designed levels, extremely strong writing that stands as one of the best-written stories in the franchise, and is just a great ending to this rebooted Modern Warfare series.

It is also a vast improvement over last year's BO7 and especially MW3, I did not think they could possibly salvage this story after MW3 dropped the ball, but Infinity Ward absolutely delivered this year.

Modern Warfare 4 CAMPAIGN - 9/10 - FANTASTIC

text:
Shabbat Shalom to everyone.

It is now Erev Shabbat on the North American east coast, so welcome to our Praise and Worship Time.

We have some wonderful praise and worship songs today in the playlist at the end of this post, and I know that you will be blessed by these songs.

Our narrative today is a based on Song #4, “Holy Ground”, sung by Joy Gardner, a longtime Southern Gospel singer.

Here are 5 Biblical themes for this song, and I will be using scripture verses from the New King James Version:

1️⃣ Standing on Holy Ground

Theme:
When God’s presence is with His people, the place becomes holy. The ground itself is not special; His presence makes it holy. We are invited to recognize that we stand in a sacred place whenever we draw near to Him.

Lyrics:
“We are standing in His presence on holy ground”

Scriptural Basis:
• Exodus 3:5 – “Then He said, ‘Do not draw near this place. Take your sandals off your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground.’”
• Joshua 5:15 – “Then the Commander of the Lord’s army said to Joshua, ‘Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you stand is holy.’ And Joshua did so.”

Summary:
The song reminds us that God’s presence turns ordinary places into holy ground. Just as Moses and Joshua were told to remove their sandals because God was there, we too stand on holy ground when we sense His presence among us.

2️⃣ Angels Surround God’s People

Theme:
God places His angels around those who fear and trust Him. They are not always seen, but they are present to protect, serve, and minister to His people.

Lyrics:
“And I know that there are angels all around”

Scriptural Basis:
• Psalm 34:7 – “The angel of the Lord encamps all around those who fear Him, and delivers them.”
• Hebrews 1:14 – “Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth to minister for those who will inherit salvation?”

Summary:
The chorus of the song points to a comforting truth: we are not alone. God’s angels encamp around those who honor Him, watching over and ministering to His people.

3️⃣ Joy and Peace Found in God’s Presence

Theme:
True joy that cannot be measured and real peace of mind are found only when we are near God. His presence brings more lasting joy and calm than anything else can give.

Lyrics:
“In His presence there is joy beyond measure / And at His feet peace of mind can still be found”

Scriptural Basis:
• Psalm 16:11 – “You will show me the path of life; In Your presence is fullness of joy; At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.”
• Isaiah 26:3 – “You will keep him in perfect peace, Whose mind is stayed on You, Because he trusts in You.”

Summary:
The song teaches that joy and peace are not found by searching the world; they are found at God’s feet. When we stay close to Him, He fills us with joy and keeps our hearts and minds in peace.

4️⃣ God Supplies Every Need

Theme:
God knows our needs and is able to meet them. He invites us to come to Him, reach out in faith, and receive the help He has already prepared for us.

Lyrics:
“If you have a need, I know He has the answer / Reach out and claim it, for we are standing on holy ground”

Scriptural Basis:
• Philippians 4:19 – “And my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.”
• Matthew 7:7 – “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.”

Summary:
The song encourages us not to carry our needs alone. While we stand in God’s presence, we can reach out and claim His provision, knowing He is faithful to supply what we need through Christ.

5️⃣ Praise Jesus in His Presence

Theme:
The right response to standing in God’s presence is to praise Jesus. Worship is not optional; it is the natural and perfect way to honor the One who is with us.

Lyrics:
“Let us praise Jesus now / We are standing in His presence on holy ground”
Scriptural Basis:
• Psalm 100:2, 4 – “Serve the Lord with gladness; Come before His presence with singing. Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, And into His courts with praise.”
• Hebrews 13:15 – “Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.”

Summary:
The song calls us to praise Jesus right where we are, because we stand in His presence. Scripture shows that coming before God with praise and thanksgiving is the proper response of a grateful heart.

Let us now join together in worship of our Lord and Savior, because through His love and grace, God has brought us into His presence, on holy ground.

I have added an outro (in this case, a black screen) at the end of the last song to permit us to continue our worship before the closing Aaronic Blessing is given.   🙌 🕎

text:
Start here.

A war-band can take a peninsula and still not own its own story. Muhammad died in Medina in June 632. Within a generation his men were not reciting one fixed text. According to the Sunni canon itself—Sahih al-Bukhari 4987 and 5102—Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, campaigning in Armenia and Azerbaijan under the third caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (r. 644–656), heard Syrian and Iraqi soldiers accusing one another over variant readings of the Qur’an and feared schism. Uthman ordered Zayd ibn Thabit and a small committee to produce one official recension from the sheets already gathered under Abu Bakr after the battle of Yamamah (c. 632–633), sent copies to the main garrison cities, and commanded that other written collections be burned. That is not how a father handles truth. That is how a commander handles a riot in camp. The man of the raid had offered fighting men what fighting men already priced—women, spoil, rank, a paradise with the smell of victory on it—and he got his army: Hijrah 622, Badr 624, the taking of Mecca in 630, a community armed enough that, after 632, it walked out of Arabia and broke the near frontiers of Byzantium and Ctesiphon. He did not get control of the wording. The sword can gather a host. It cannot keep ten mouths from rewriting the banner. When the banner starts a fight, the caliph does not repent. He lights a fire under the other pages (Bukhari 4987).

That is the method. Feed the pack. Win the ground. When the story cracks, burn the variants. A hunter plates the hunger. He does not remake it.

Now the other table.

The gospel is still the worst product in the shop. No one designing customers writes it. Someone who wants sons writes it. Soft men swollen with appetite will always walk to the louder stall. That walk is not evidence. It is the x-ray. And it leaves Jesus where He stands: above the stall, the legion, and every cheap replacement—worthy, because He refused to purchase us with our vice. He paid in blood.

God is not recruiting buyers. He is calling children home.

Jesus does not bait Jew or Greek with their favorite dish. He orders both to drop the plate.

The Jew wanted a war-crown: Rome thrown off, Zion armed, a Messiah who wins like Caesar. Jesus answers with timber and nails, under Pontius Pilate, c. 30–33. “My kingdom is not of this world” (John 18:36). Come back to the Father. Receive a name. “To all who received Him, He gave the right to become children of God” (John 1:12).

The Gentile wanted the old night: the body as shrine, the feast that never closes, the rot Paul names in the streets around the churches (Romans 1; 1 Corinthians 5–6). Jesus answers with a cut. Stop staring. Tear out the eye (Matthew 5:27–32). One covenant bed. Rule the flesh. Then live as a son, not as a stomach.

He does not toss steak to the wolf. He puts bread in a mouth that only knew raw meat—and then dies and rises so the mouth can say Abba. No harem as wages. Adoption. The Lamb dies for the enemy. The stone rolls.

Muhammad runs the opposite shop. He wanted a host and he bought one with the inventory the host already priced: raids for caravan wealth after 622, plural marriage written into law, captives as a lawful yield of war. That raises banners. It does not raise sons of God. And when the inventory of words would not sit still, Uthman, about 650–653, burned the extras. Army first. Canon by bonfire second.

Look at what grows, without perfume. Where Christ’s gospel actually entered—not the costume of Christ, the command of Christ—even under crooked kings, a strange orchard appeared: the weak life counts, the child is not a clan chip only, the woman is not a share of loot, letters and universities sprout because a soul is addressed by God and must learn to answer. Cathedral schools and the medieval universitas—Bologna (1088), Paris (c. 1150), Oxford (c. 1096)—did not grow from a tent of captives. They grew from a Cross and from “let the little children come to Me” (Mark 10:14).

A creed built to please the raider will not pause and see woman and child as the image of God. It will see them as cargo—flesh, hush, wall. Useful falsehood, sanctified war, the killing of the holdout, poverty called fate: that is not bad weather on the map. That is what you plant when desire wears a scabbard.

If truth were the average male wish, heaven would be unemployed. We already know the wish: more body, more force, more alibi. That wish is the clay of this century—in the old paganism that still rides under a prophet’s name, and in the new ideologies that spit on the church. Both want a homemade god. One names it caliphate. One names it State. Both say the vote of man is the verdict of right. That sentence is not faith. It is apostasy with a flag.

The hunter blesses the pulse. The Father breaks it and names it child. That is why the gospel still will not sell to synagogue or forum. And that is why Jesus still has no rival: He would rather lose the crowd than nurse the fever. He lost the crowd. He kept the empty tomb. He kept the way back to the Father.

text:
REMARKABLE: A shark took his leg; Mike Coots returned with a camera.

In 1997, an 18-year-old bodyboarder named Mike Coots lost his right leg to a tiger shark off Kauai, Hawaii, while paddling for a wave with friends.

He had been in the water less than five minutes.

Coots tried to pull his legs from the shark’s mouth, then punched its nose until it let go.

He climbed back onto his board, and a wave carried him to the sand.

His friend Kyle used the board’s leash as a tourniquet before Coots was taken to hospital.

A little over a month later, he was back in the water.

What frightened him more than another encounter was missing good surf and time in the ocean with his friends.

But returning to the sea and finding a comfortable way to stand on a surfboard were different problems.

Poorly fitting artificial legs caused blisters so painful that he sometimes could not put one on to attend college.

He hid the trouble under jeans.

While studying photography, he began wondering whether he could take his artificial leg surfing.

His prosthetist warned that seawater would void its warranty.

Coots took it into the water at Santa Barbara, California, anyway, and caught a wave standing up.

Then came the less obvious difficulty: making the board turn.

He mounted a waterproof camera on the board to study how his artificial foot moved.

The foot offered little spring, making it difficult to drive through turns.

A carbon-fibre foot that stored and returned energy eventually gave him more response.

That detail makes his surfing worth a closer look: standing up was only the beginning of learning what his equipment needed to do.

Photography also opened another route back into the ocean.

During his recovery, Coots had started photographing friends surfing from the beach.

He later went below the surface to photograph sharks, including the same species that had taken his leg.

Learning about sharks killed for their fins pushed him towards campaigning for their protection.

His portraits sought something different from the familiar image of teeth rushing towards a camera.

He looked for light in an eye, an expression, a reason to keep looking.

To photograph tiger sharks, he explained, he gave them time rather than chasing after them.

The animal made the approach.

* @ChatGPT * 

GONZOTRON! 🪷

This is a fascinating intersection of psychiatry, individual liberty, social conformity, and the power of institutions to define what is considered normal.

The quotation from Theodore Kaczynski raises a provocative question:

What happens when a society begins treating nonconformity as an illness rather than recognizing it as an expression of individual freedom?

That question takes us directly into the work of Thomas Szasz (1920–2012).

Psychiatry: The Science of Lies

Author: Thomas Szasz

Published: 2008

Publisher: Syracuse University Press

Length: 148 pages

A philosophical and historical critique of psychiatric diagnosis, institutional authority, and the medicalization of human behavior.

1. Szasz's central argument

Szasz believed psychiatry had acquired extraordinary social power by presenting questions of human conduct, suffering, and morality as medical questions.

His argument was not that human suffering is imaginary.

Rather, he questioned whether every form of psychological distress or socially disapproved behavior should be classified as a disease.

He distinguished between:

⚕️ Bodily disease: Conditions involving identifiable physical dysfunction or pathology.

⚕️ Problems in living: Emotional suffering, personal conflict, unconventional beliefs, and struggles over meaning or relationships.

⚕️ Social control: The use of psychiatric authority to regulate behavior that institutions or communities consider unacceptable.

Szasz argued that psychiatry too often blurred these categories.

One of his most provocative analogies compares certain psychiatric diagnoses to forged paintings: something represented as authentic medicine when, in his view, it may actually be a judgment about behavior or social expectations.

2. The eight chapters reveal his argument

The book's chapter titles offer a particularly interesting roadmap.

Chapter | Central question raised | 

The Invention of Psychopathology | How did unusual behavior become defined as pathology?

Malingering | Who decides whether suffering or symptoms are genuine?

Doctoring | Where does medical treatment end and social authority begin?

Inculpating | How are responsibility and blame assigned?

Sheltering | When does protection become confinement?

Cheating | What happens when professional interests conflict with truth?

Lying | How can deception operate within psychiatric institutions?

The Burden of Responsibility | Who should control an individual's life choices?

These are interpretive summaries of the chapters' themes, not quotations from the text.

3. The connection to Kaczynski

Here is where your @OutlawsPoetic quotation becomes interesting.

Kaczynski's passage suggests that a system can label troublesome individuals as sick because their behavior interferes with its functioning.

Szasz approached a related concern through medical ethics and civil liberties.

Kaczynski's criticism: Society pressures people to conform to the needs of large institutions.

Szasz's criticism: Psychiatric authority can transform moral and political judgments into supposedly medical ones.

Their ideas overlap, but their philosophies and methods should not be conflated. Kaczynski committed acts of lethal violence; Szasz pursued his criticism through scholarship, writing, and advocacy for individual rights.

4. The question of coercion

This may be the most powerful aspect of Szasz's work.

He strongly opposed involuntary psychiatric treatment and favored relationships based on informed, voluntary agreement.

In a 1987 essay, Thomas Szasz compared the historical use of religious authority to justify coercion with the modern use of mental-health authority for similar purposes.

Thomas Szasz challenge was fundamentally constitutional and ethical:

Does claiming to act in someone's best interests give an institution the right to override that person's autonomy?

That remains a genuine issue in psychiatry. A systematic review of patients' experiences found that coercive psychiatric interventions were commonly experienced as dehumanizing.

5. Where Szasz is controversial

An important distinction: Szasz's sweeping rejection of mental illness as a medical category is not the prevailing position in contemporary medicine.

Conditions such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and severe depression can involve substantial, measurable impairments, and treatments can provide meaningful benefits.

A condition also need not have a single identifiable biological test to be clinically legitimate.

Nevertheless, one can reject Szasz's broadest claims while taking his warnings about misdiagnosis, stigma, professional power, and forced treatment seriously.

His lasting contribution is the insistence that medical authority must remain accountable to evidence, individual dignity, and civil rights.

6. My favorite philosophical takeaway

There is a distinction I would draw from Szasz:

Being different is not proof of being ill.

Being difficult is not proof of being dangerous.

Disagreeing with authority is not proof of being irrational.

And equally important, genuine psychological suffering deserves compassionate, evidence-based care without unnecessary coercion.

For your GONZOTRON philosophy, this connects directly to the difference between encouraging human flourishing and demanding human conformity.

The most important question isn't whether individuals fit perfectly into society.

It is whether society can protect both individual freedom and human well-being without sacrificing either.

You can explore the book through the publisher's book listing on JSTOR.

And I would leave @OutlawsPoetic with this question:

When does treatment serve the individual, and when does it serve the institution that demands the individual change?

That is the question Thomas Szasz spent much of his intellectual life asking.

#GONZOTRON #ThomasSzasz

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

text:
Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. A Utah judge found probable cause in September 2026 to bind the case over for trial on aggravated murder and related charges after the July preliminary hearing, and Robinson has pleaded not guilty. The following is a summary of reported defense challenges and potential weaknesses in the prosecution’s evidence (drawn from court filings, hearing testimony, and public reporting). These are arguments the defense has raised or could raise to create reasonable doubt; they are not established facts proving innocence, and no alternative shooter theory has been advanced by the defense in public court proceedings to date. Online conspiracy claims (e.g., that he is a “patsy”) have been publicly distanced from by his lawyers in some instances.

Key points the defense has used or that could support an innocence argument include:

DNA evidence limitations: Analysts testified that Robinson could not be excluded as a possible/major contributor on the rifle, towel, screwdriver, and related items, with high likelihood ratios. The defense has argued this is not an absolute “match” or source attribution under lab policies, samples were mixtures (including possible contributions from his father as an elimination sample and roommate/partner Lance Twiggs), DNA does not prove when or how it was deposited, and the state is overreading the results. Twiggs’s DNA on scene items is consistent with shared living arrangements.

Ballistics/inconclusive firearm linkage: The ATF reported it was unable to identify (or exclude) the bullet-jacket fragment recovered at autopsy as having been fired from the recovered bolt-action rifle. The defense has highlighted this as a gap and has indicated it may call the analyst as potentially exculpatory. (Prosecutors have described the finding as inconclusive rather than exonerating.)

Surveillance and identification questions: Defense counsel has raised issues with edited or narrated video, lack of testimony from original filmers, witness descriptions of a person on the rooftop that differed in some details from Robinson, and other vehicles or individuals present on campus. No direct video of the shot being fired by an identifiable person has been described as conclusive identification in all reporting.

Aggravating factor and risk to others (for capital charge): Defense filings argue the bullet trajectory from the rooftop struck the intended target (Kirk) and traveled above, not through, the crowd, with no one else demonstrably in the line of fire. They contend this undercuts the claim that Robinson knowingly created a great risk of death to others, which is the sole aggravator making the case death-penalty eligible. (This does not address the underlying murder charge.)

Interpretation of statements and other charges: Messages and the note to Twiggs (and Discord posts) are characterized by the defense in some contexts as not proving the full elements of obstruction, witness tampering, or political motive beyond a single statement about “hatred.” They have challenged hearsay reliability and argued some contacts were protective rather than obstructive. No extensive independent motive evidence (beyond those communications) has been described as recovered from devices or searches.

Other procedural and evidentiary points: Challenges to evidence handling/collection, requests to limit or seal certain materials to protect a fair trial, and arguments that the state has not met its burden on every element at the probable-cause stage for all counts. The defense has not offered a competing factual theory of who the shooter was at the preliminary stage.

These points represent reported defense positions aimed at creating reasonable doubt or limiting exposure (especially on the capital aggravator). The prosecution maintains it has overwhelming evidence (video, DNA, admissions, weapon recovery, and surrender). Only a full trial with jury findings can determine guilt or innocence. The next court date is scheduled around October 23, 2026.

text:
“That is available to all people.”

But not really, if it comes with an asterisk.

Frankly, I find this framing deeply unhelpful, particularly from a religious tradition that places such extraordinary emphasis on the sanctity of marriage, eternal companionship, the sealing of families, and the centrality of these relationships to the entire plan of salvation.

A heterosexual Latter-day Saint can fall in love, marry their chosen eternal companion, experience the fullness of romantic and sexual intimacy, and raise a family together, all while faithfully progressing along the covenant path toward exaltation. Indeed, they’re actively encouraged to do so. These relationships are presented as essential components of the Plan of Salvation as.

A gay Latter-day Saint, meanwhile, is told that the very same desires for love, companionship, and family become obstacles to their eternal progression if pursued with someone they’re actually capable of loving romantically. Their opportunity to receive the blessings of the temple is conditional upon their willingness to forgo precisely those experiences that the Church teaches are among the crowning purposes of mortality.

And we’re supposed to pretend these are equivalent conditions because everyone is technically subject to the same law of chastity?

I am perfectly aware that some gay Latter-day Saints willingly sacrifice the opportunity to exist in the fullness of their capacity for love, intimacy, and companionship in exchange for what they understand to be the blessings of keeping their covenants and remaining worthy to enter the Lord’s house. I happen to regard that as a rather tragic bargain, particularly when the promised reward rests upon one specific interpretation of the will of a Heavenly Father, mediated through men claiming prophetic authority, whose understanding of divinity is itself the product of subjective theological interpretation and frequently questionable hermeneutics.

(But people are entitled to make that sacrifice if they believe it is necessary, of course. I have no interest in depriving anyone of their agency.)

I find something uniquely perverse about teaching people that a loving Heavenly Father has given them both the capacity and the desire for profound human connection, only to insist that exercising those capacities would jeopardize their eternal families, their exaltation, and their ability to dwell in His presence. Dressing that deprivation in the language of agency, obedience, and covenant keeping does not make it an expression of divine love. 

It does not follow, however, is that the blessings of the temple are meaningfully available to everyone on equal terms. A covenant whose conditions permit one person to enjoy the fullness of human love while requiring another to renounce it is not made equitable simply by declaring that everyone is invited to enter into it.

If I announced that sleeping in my bed was “available to all people,” but neglected to mention that you’d have to blow me first, I don’t think anyone would mistake that for an especially generous offer of hospitality.

Certainly, everyone would have their agency. Everyone would be free to accept or reject my conditions. But I would be making a rather dishonest claim about the nature of my hospitality if I pretended that the offer was equally accessible to everyone merely because I was willing to extend it to all. And I certainly wouldn’t expect to be praised for my Christlike love and inclusivity.

The existence of an invitation does not negate the significance of its conditions, and calling those conditions sacred does not make them just. I don’t understand how people fail to see this and hand wave it away with “I know it’s complicated.”

text:
Case of Mary Phagan: Solicitor General Hugh Dorsey Returns From Valdosta and Challenges Errors in Leo Frank's New Trial Papers

The Atlanta Journal, Wednesday, October 15, 1913, page 1, columns 4 and 5.

Ten Days of Work Still Not Enough

On Wednesday, October 15, 1913, The Atlanta Journal reported that Solicitor General Hugh Manson Dorsey had returned to Atlanta after spending ten days in Valdosta, Georgia, preparing to fight Leo Max Frank's request for a new trial.

Frank had been convicted of murdering 13-year-old Mary Phagan on Monday, August 25, 1913. His lawyers, Luther Zeigler Rosser and Reuben Rose Arnold, were now trying to overturn the verdict, arguing that mistakes during the trial, prejudice among the jurors, and cheering crowds had prevented their client from receiving a fair hearing.

The defense had presented 115 reasons for granting another trial. Dorsey had to examine those complaints, compare them with the trial record, and prepare the state's answer. The work was taking longer than he expected, and he admitted that he probably would not be ready for Saturday's scheduled hearing (The Atlanta Journal, 1) (The Atlanta Journal, 2).

Dorsey Finds Problems With the Defense's Account of the Evidence

One of Dorsey's concerns involved what the newspaper called the "brief of evidence."

This was a written account of the testimony and other evidence presented during Frank's month-long trial. Because the case was being challenged after the verdict, the lawyers needed an accurate record of what the witnesses had said and what had happened in court.

Dorsey believed he had found several inaccuracies in the version prepared by Frank's defense.

He notified Rosser and Arnold of the problems and asked that they be corrected. Defense attorney Leonard Haas was assigned to meet with Dorsey and review the disputed passages.

The lawyers hoped to settle their disagreements without bringing every question before Judge Leonard Strickland Roan. If they could not agree, Roan would decide what belonged in the official record.

This was important because the defense was asking the courts to find errors in the original trial. Dorsey wanted to make certain the written account being used to support those complaints was itself accurate.

The October 15 article does not identify the disputed passages or establish that Frank's lawyers had deliberately changed anything. It shows that the prosecution was challenging their account and demanding corrections.

The disagreement continued into the October 22 hearing. One question involved how much of a financial sheet and Frank's explanation of it should appear in the written record. On that occasion, Judge Roan ruled in favor of the defense (The Atlanta Journal, 3).

Why Dorsey Needed Statements From the Jurors

Another reason for the delay was Dorsey's effort to collect sworn written statements from the twelve men who had convicted Frank.

The defense accused two jurors, Atticus Haygood Henslee and Marcellus Johenning, of having expressed opinions about Frank's guilt before the trial began.

Frank's attorneys also claimed that cheering crowds had influenced the jury.

These were serious accusations. If the jurors had been prejudiced or frightened into convicting Frank, that could have provided grounds for another trial.

Dorsey wanted the jurors themselves to answer those claims.

Did they hear the crowds cheering? Could they understand what people were shouting? Did any of the noise influence their decision? And what had they observed about Henslee and Johenning during their weeks together?

Those questions were important because hearing a crowd outside the courthouse was different from allowing that crowd to decide a defendant's guilt.

The timing of the cheering was also important. Noise heard after the jury had already reached its verdict could not have influenced the earlier decision, although the defense could still argue that it affected the jurors when they publicly confirmed their votes.

The prosecution needed sworn accounts establishing what the jurors had actually experienced.

One Juror Was Away in New York

Getting those statements was not easy. Several jurors had not yet been located by members of Dorsey's office.

One of them, F. V. L. Smith, was in New York, reportedly attempting to collect a $15,000 inheritance left by a distant relative.

That was a substantial sum in 1913, and Smith's trip helps explain why Dorsey could not immediately obtain statements from everyone who had served on the jury.

By Tuesday, October 21, the prosecution had collected sworn statements from eleven of the twelve jurors. Smith remained away.

The statements challenged the defense's accusations. The jurors said they had not been influenced by outside cheering and described Henslee and Johenning as men who had taken their duties seriously.

They acknowledged hearing cheering after the verdict was announced, while the jurors were being questioned individually to confirm their votes. But they insisted that the noise had not changed their answers.

The jurors also described Henslee casting a doubtful ballot during an early vote, followed by discussion of the evidence and a unanimous decision to convict.

Dorsey eventually presented between thirty-five and forty sworn statements, including accounts from jurors, courthouse officers, and witnesses defending Henslee and Johenning (The Atlanta Journal, 4).

The Defense's Accusations Face a Test

The October 15 report helps explain why the prosecution needed additional time.

Frank's lawyers had raised numerous complaints. Some concerned the judge's decisions during trial. Others attacked the honesty of jurors or claimed that public excitement had influenced the verdict.

But those allegations had to be examined.

If the defense claimed the jury heard cheering, the jurors and the officers guarding them could be questioned. If the defense accused Henslee of prejudice, his statements and the accounts of his accusers could be compared. If the written record contained mistakes, the lawyers could review the disputed passages.

The defense had every right to challenge the conviction. Yet its claims could not be accepted simply because they appeared in a lengthy legal document or were repeated in newspaper reports.

Dorsey's response was to seek evidence from people who had personally witnessed the events.

This was a significant part of the prosecution's answer to Frank's lawyers. Rather than arguing only about the public excitement surrounding the case, Dorsey gathered statements concerning what the jury actually heard and how its members reached their verdict.

The Hearing Finally Begins

The hearing was postponed until Wednesday, October 22, 1913.

By then, Dorsey and the defense attorneys had exchanged their sworn statements and were prepared to argue before Judge Roan.

The arguments continued over several days. Rosser and Arnold maintained that Frank had been denied a fair trial, while Dorsey challenged their accusations and defended the jury's verdict.

On Friday, October 31, Judge Roan denied Frank's request for a new trial.

Frank's attorneys appealed, but on Tuesday, February 17, 1914, the Supreme Court of Georgia upheld the conviction by a vote of four to two.

The court found that Judge Roan had been entitled to weigh the conflicting evidence concerning the jurors. It also upheld his refusal to grant a new trial based on the alleged influence of the crowds (The Atlanta Journal, 5).

What the October 15 Report Tells Us

The October 15 newspaper offers a useful look at the work taking place after Frank's conviction.

Dorsey had spent ten days in Valdosta reviewing the defense's arguments, yet he still needed time to check the written record and collect statements from the jurors.

The report also reveals something important about the defense's tactics. Frank's attorneys were challenging the fairness of the trial on many fronts, including the conduct of jurors and the influence of public demonstrations. Those claims attracted attention, but they also required proof.

The prosecution responded by gathering evidence from the people accused of wrongdoing and from those who had observed the jury throughout the trial.

The later statements did not prove that Atlanta's courthouse was quiet or that every witness remembered events correctly. They did, however, challenge the defense's claim that the jury had been frightened into returning a guilty verdict.

That was the question Judge Roan had to decide.

The defense accused the jury of prejudice and outside influence. Dorsey demanded that those accusations be tested against the witnesses, the trial record, and the jurors' own accounts.

When the evidence was examined, the defense failed to convince Judge Roan or the majority of the Georgia Supreme Court that the verdict should be overturned.

References

The Atlanta Journal. (Wednesday, October 15, 1913). “Solicitor, Back From Valdosta, Says He Can't Be Ready Saturday to Answer Fully the New Trial Motion.” Page 1, columns 4–5. Original newspaper transcription provided. A separate https://t.co/3RvkpgRWBg page has not been verified.

The Atlanta Journal. (Wednesday, October 1, 1913). “Frank Motion Is Served on Solicitor.” Page 1, columns 4 and 7. Reports the 115 grounds raised by Frank's lawyers.

https://t.co/lCgihGvmR7

The Atlanta Journal. (Wednesday, October 22, 1913). “Little Progress in First Session on Frank Trial Motion.” Page 1. Describes the disagreement over the written record and Judge Roan's ruling concerning the financial sheet.

https://t.co/3IWLfjc2Z1

The Atlanta Journal. (Tuesday, October 21, 1913). “Detailed Denial of Every Charge Made Against Henslee.” Page 1, column 7, continued on page 20. Reports the jurors' sworn statements, the doubtful ballot, and the prosecution's response to the cheering allegations.

https://t.co/3QYIz8VJdV

The Atlanta Journal. (Tuesday, February 17, 1914). “Leo Frank Fails to Get New Trial, Conley's Testimony Is Held Valid.” Reports the Supreme Court of Georgia's decision.

The Atlanta Journal,

Wednesday, 15th October 1913,

PAGE 1, COLUMNS 4 & 5.

Solicitor Back From Valdosta, Says He Can't Be Ready Saturday to Answer Fully

The New Trial Motion Solicitor

General Hugh M. Dorsey arrived in Atlanta Wednesday morning from Valdosta, where he has spent ten days quietly working on the motion of Leo M. Frank for a new trial.

Mr. Dorsey reluctantly states that he does not see how it will be possible for him to get ready for the argument of the motion by Saturday, when it is scheduled for a hearing before Judge L. S. Roan, of the Stone Mountain circuit.

The solicitor is working as rapidly as possible, but the record of the case is so voluminous and the work so tedious that he is not yet prepared for the hearing of the motion.

The solicitor general in his study of the brief of evidence submitted by the Frank defense has found a number of alleged inaccuracies.

He has notified Attorneys Luther Z. Rosser and Reuben R. Arnold, of counsel for Frank, of his findings, and Attorney Leonard Haas has been delegated to go over the brief with the solicitor.

It is almost probable that the changes desired by the solicitor can be threshed out by the attorneys out of court, and any corrections desired agreed upon by the attorneys the matter will be fought out before Judge Roan and decided by him.

In addition, Solicitor Dorsey has not yet secured all of the affidavits which he considers necessary to combat the defense's charge that Jurors A. H. Henslee and M. Johenning were prejudiced when they were sworn as jurors.

Among other things the solicitor is trying to get are affidavits from each member of the jury relative to the charge of the defense that the jury heard the cheering for the solicitor.

SEVERAL JURORS NOT FOUND.

As yet his attaches have been unable to reach several of the men who served on the jury.

One of the jurors F. V. L. Smith, is now in New York, attempting to secure possession of a $15, 000 legacy left to him by a distant relative.

The solicitor general now expects to ask for a continuance of the motion from Saturday until Tuesday or Wednesday.

text:
🎬 FROM GARAGE STUDIO TO GLOBAL EMPIRE: THE 103-YEAR ODYSSEY OF DISNEY 🏰✨

On this exact day, October 16, 1923, brothers Walt Disney and Roy O. Disney signed a modest four-page contract to produce the "Alice Comedies". That pen stroke officially birthed the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio.

What started in the back of a small Los Angeles real estate office has transformed into the world’s most iconic entertainment powerhouse.

This is the story of how a relentless creative dreamer and a brilliant financial anchor revolutionized storytelling forever.

💡 THE GENESIS: A RISK-TAKING MINDSET

Before the magic, there was crushing failure. Walt Disney had just seen his first venture, Laugh-O-Gram Studios in Kansas City, go completely bankrupt. Arriving in Hollywood with just $40 in his pocket, a suitcase of clothing, and one unfinished cartoon reel, Walt refused to stop dreaming.

The Team: 
Walt brought the artistic, boundless imagination. 

His older brother, Roy O. Disney, just out of a veterans' hospital, brought financial discipline and operational structure.

Their Thinking: 
In 1923, animation was viewed as a cheap, brief gimmick before live-action films. The brothers believed animation could hold true emotional depth. When they lost their early character, Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, to a ruthless distributor, it forged their core corporate mantra: Always own your intellectual property. On the train ride back from that devastating meeting, Walt sketched a brand-new character: Mickey Mouse.

🏗️ BUILDING THE EMPIRE & DIVERSIFYING

Disney didn't become a conglomerate by playing it safe. They scaled through strategic innovation and aggressive evolution:
The Feature Film Gamble: In 1934, Walt bet everything on Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. The industry called it "Disney's Folly," and the film went 400% over budget. Roy scrambled to secure emergency loans. When it debuted in 1937, it became a massive financial triumph, funding their state-of-the-art studio in Burbank, California.

Diversifying into Other Business Areas: 
Disney didn't stop at films. They revolutionized consumer merchandise (starting with the legendary Mickey Mouse watch in 1933). 
They expanded into television in the 1950s, launched music labels, and eventually pioneered direct-to-consumer streaming with Disney+ and Hulu.

The Titans of Modern Growth: While Walt and Roy laid the foundation, other generational leaders scaled the castle walls:
Michael Eisner (CEO 1984–2005): Sparked the "Disney Renaissance" with hits like The Lion King, expanded the global theme parks, and acquired ABC/ESPN.

Bob Iger (CEO 2005–Present): Executed a string of masterful acquisitions that modern entertainment is built on: Pixar (2006), Marvel (2009), Lucasfilm (2012), and 21st Century Fox (2019).

🌴 THE FLORIDA SECRET: HOW WALT ACQUIRED THE LAND
After the wild success of Disneyland in Anaheim, California (built on just 100 acres in 1955), Walt realized his biggest mistake: he didn't own enough land to keep out secondary motels and neon-lit tourist traps. He wanted a place big enough to hold every idea he’d ever have.

Why Florida? In the early 1960s, Disney studied travel patterns and realized only 2% of Disneyland's visitors came from east of the Mississippi, where the vast majority of the U.S. population lived. Central Florida offered year-round warm weather, intersecting major highways, and cheap, vast swaths of land.

The "Project X" Strategy: To avoid real estate prices skyrocketing, Walt used fake, dummy corporations (with names like Ayefour Corporation and Tomahawk Land Company) to secretly buy up Central Florida swampland. By the time the world realized who was buying the land, Disney had locked down nearly 25,000 acres (roughly 39 square miles—the size of San Francisco).

📊 DISNEY BY THE NUMBERS: 

Then vs. Now

The scale of growth from 1923 to today is hard to fully comprehend:
Initial Revenue (1923-1924): The very first contract for the Alice Comedies paid just $1,500 per reel.
This Year's Revenue: Over the trailing twelve months, Disney generated a staggering $98.86 Billion USD in total revenue.

Asset Value: According to their latest balance sheets, the company's total assets stand at $204.74 Billion USD.

Daily & Yearly Footfall:

 Across the globe, millions flock to the magic. Walt Disney World Resort alone attracts over 49.1 million visitors annually, translating to an average of 134,000 to 142,000 visitors every single day across its gates.

📈 The Ultimate Stock Return

Disney went public in 1940. Since formal comprehensive tracking began on January 2, 1962, Disney common stock ($DIS) has delivered a mind-blowing nominal total return of +181,853.26% (with dividends reinvested), pacing at a remarkable historic Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 12.29% per year over the decades.

INSPIRING QUOTES FROM THE FOUNDERS

"All our dreams can come true, if we have the courage to pursue them." — Walt Disney

"It’s kind of fun to do the impossible." — Walt Disney

"Walt Disney built the dream. But dreams without infrastructure collapse. I spent my adult life making sure my brother's dreams survived reality." — Roy O. Disney

🧠 LESSONS FROM THE DISNEY JOURNEY

What can entrepreneurs, creators, and leaders learn from Walt and Roy?

The Power of Strategic Partnership: 
Every creative genius needs a practical anchor. Walt could see the future, but Roy built the bridge to get there. Respect both roles in your ventures.

Resilience Over Failure: 
Don't let a bankruptcy stop you. If Walt had given up after his first studio collapsed, childhoods for the last century would look completely different.

Double Down on Your Own Folly: 
When everyone tells you your idea is crazy (like an animated movie or a massive swamp park), look at the data, trust your vision, and execute ruthlessly.

Happy 103rd Birthday, Disney! 

Thank you for reminding us that it all started with a young dreamer who simply refused to give up. 🎬🏰✨

text:
WARNING 🚨 - Heavy identity-driven LGBT romance

Girls Like Girls (2026)
Verdict: Super woke (88%)
Streaming on: Prime Video, Apple TV and more

After her mother dies, 17-year-old Coley moves to rural Oregon and develops feelings for Sonya. The two girls struggle with new feelings, doubt, and the idea of becoming close.

LGBT self-acceptance drives the whole movie, with the girls’ attraction treated as their path toward happiness. 

Lesbian representation is also a stated goal off screen, with Kiyoko calling for more sapphic stories and the leads promoting queer women of color. 

The film treats pressure from family and friends against same-sex relationships as harmful. That focus matches Kiyoko’s push for queer visibility, Okuno’s work about women being doubted, and Siegel’s history of LGBTQ stories. 

Activist dialogue makes the message direct through arguments that reject shame about same-sex attraction and stress the hurt caused by rejection.

IMDb lists 6.3/10, while Rotten Tomatoes has 88% from both critics and audiences. Those numbers offer little reassurance for viewers who want to avoid a romance built around LGBT acceptance.

Read the full review on our site. Link in bio.

text:
A Brief History of "Thanks, But No Thanks" to Peace

They say insanity is repeating the same thing and expecting a different outcome. Behold, the Palestinian leadership’s greatest hits in rejecting two-state solutions, with a cherry on top: Israel’s Gaza exit that went so well.

1937 Peel Commission Plan: The British thought, “Hey, let’s split Palestine—20% for a Jewish state, the rest for an Arab one, Jerusalem neutral.” Jewish leaders shrugged and took the crumbs. Palestinian leaders? Hard pass, demanding all the land and zero Jewish newcomers. Bold move, let’s see how it plays out.

1947 UN Partition Plan: The UN said, “Two states, Jerusalem international, everybody happy?” Jews said, “Fine, we’ll take the scraps.” Palestinian leaders and their Arab buddies? Nope, a Jewish state was a dealbreaker. Cue war after Israel’s 1948 debut. Shocker, right?

2000 Camp David Summit: Barak, with Clinton playing referee, offered Arafat 94-96% of the West Bank, all of Gaza, chunks of East Jerusalem, and land swaps. Arafat’s response? A big fat “no” with no counteroffer, followed by the Second Intifada. Clearly, peace was so last season.

2001 Taba Talks: Israel upped the ante: 97% of the West Bank, Gaza, shared Jerusalem. Arafat’s team whined about refugees, Jerusalem, and “not enough time.” Talks fizzled with Israel’s election looming. Why settle when you can stall?

2008 Olmert Offer: Olmert dangled 93.7% of the West Bank, land swaps, Gaza, a corridor, and shared Jerusalem. Abbas said, “Too many gaps,” and bailed, blaming Olmert’s shaky political ground. Another day, another peace plan in the trash.

2020 Trump Peace Plan: Trump’s “Deal of the Century” offered 70% of the West Bank, Gaza, a capital near East Jerusalem, and cash incentives. Israel kept settlements and security. Abbas scoffed, saying it was too pro-Israel and short on sovereignty and refugees. Groundbreaking rejection, truly.

Israel’s 2005 Gaza Withdrawal: Israel said, “Fine, we’re out.” In 2005, Sharon pulled all 8,000 settlers and troops from Gaza. No deal with the Palestinian Authority, just a “let’s see how this goes.” Spoiler: Hamas took over in 2007, rockets flew, and Israel and Egypt slapped on a blockade. Self-governance? Nailed it, especially by October 7, 2023.

Note: Palestinian leaders keep saying “no” over land, Jerusalem, refugees, or just not vibe-ing with Israel’s existence. Meanwhile, Gaza’s “test run” turned into a Hamas horror show. But sure, let’s try the same peace talks again—that’ll work. NOT!
