text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 92 to 98 (Week 14): Taste and Smell Begin:  🌱 Pregnancy Days 92 to 98 (Week 14)  Taste buds are forming on your baby's tongue this week. Months from now, flavors from the food you eat will reach your baby in the water world. Could your baby's first taste of a family meal come before the first bite?
👶 Where your baby is this week
If conception happened around day 14, your baby is 78 to 84 days old this week. This week the second trimester begins. Taste buds are forming on your baby's tongue, and the parts of the nose and brain that will one day smell are developing too. Your baby is swallowing small amounts of the fluid in the water world.
Red blood cells are now being made in the spleen as well as the liver. The neck is becoming more defined, so the head sits more upright on the body. A soft, fine hair called lanugo may begin to appear on the skin, and the thyroid gland is beginning its work.
The outer genitals are becoming clearer, though they are not always easy to see on a scan yet. Your baby is almost 3 1/2 inches long from crown to rump and weighs about 1 1/2 ounces, about the size of a peach.

🤰 Your body this week
Continue your folic acid, 400 micrograms each day. Your baby is growing fast in the second trimester, and every new cell needs it.
For many women, this is when energy returns and nausea fades. Your appetite may grow, and a small bump may show. Good food, lots of water, and a daily walk carry you far. Your body is making more blood, so keep eating iron-rich foods with fruit or vegetables high in vitamin C.
You may notice a stuffy nose, heartburn, or a dull ache low in your back. Check with your doctor before you take anything for them. Ask your doctor or midwife about anything you are unsure of, because I am not a doctor.

🎶 Why singing, not talking
Words need a listener who knows their meaning. A sung melody, its rhythm, and its pitch reach a child before understanding does. That is why lullabies and nursery rhymes are older than any classroom.
In GUP songs you hear baby music with intent: the calm of lullabies, the repetition of nursery rhymes, and phonic songs that grow into reading. Kids music starts here, in your own voice.

🔬 Science and sound
Your baby's senses are developing one by one, and hearing comes later, in the second half of pregnancy. The studies of babies recognizing their mother's voice were done after that, not in Week 14.
The song is still a habit for you rather than a lesson your baby hears. Build the home now, and your voice will be its sound when hearing arrives.

🎵 One song, three ways
First thing each day, hear it with closed eyes and praise God for the senses He is building. At lunchtime, hum it through headphones. Each evening, journal the phonograms (phonic songs) you hear, then add your favorites to the First Sounds list.
Dad, take your turn with headphones. Let the sound of your voice be part of the home your baby is born into.

🙏 Pray and remember
✝️ The psalmist invites us to taste and see that the Lord is good (Psalm 34:8, CPDV).
🎂 Born September 29, 1951: Michelle Bachelet. A pediatrician, she became Chile's first female president in 2006. Taste and see that the Lord is good, and this week your baby's taste and smell begin.
This week God begins the taste buds of your child.
"Father God, thank You for the senses You are building in our child. Let our home be full of good things to taste, smell, and hear. Let our lullabies come first in our baby's memory. In Jesus' name, amen."

✅ WEEK-14 CHECKLIST
This week I took folic acid every day and ate a colorful plate. I kept the three ways, added to our First Sounds list, and Dad hummed with me.

➡️ NEXT WEEK
Rolling and Flipping.

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 14 (Days 92 to 98): Taste and Smell Begin

💊 Folic Acid: The Second Trimester
The second trimester is a season of fast growth. Your baby will grow from about 3 1/2 inches to over a foot long from head to heel before it ends. All that growth means new cells, and folic acid helps each one form correctly.
Four hundred micrograms a day remains the usual amount, whether in a prenatal vitamin or on its own. Most doctors want the prenatal vitamin to continue through pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Fourteen weeks in, the habit is strong. Keep the bottle and the headphones in one spot. Each habit cues the other.

👀 Week 14 at a Glance
Week 14 is pregnancy days 92 to 98, counted from the first day of your last period. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 78 and 84 days old this week.
This is the week the second trimester begins. Taste buds form on the tongue, the parts that will smell are developing, red blood cells form in the spleen, the neck becomes more defined, and the outer genitals become clearer. Your baby is almost 3 1/2 inches long from crown to rump, about the size of a peach.

🗓️ The Week, Day by Day

🗓️ Days 78 to 81 (Pregnancy Days 92 to 95): Taste Buds and an Upright Head
The second trimester begins, and taste buds are forming on the tongue and the roof of the mouth. By days 80 and 81 the spleen joins the liver in making red blood cells. The neck lengthens, and the head sits more upright.

🗓️ Days 82 to 84 (Pregnancy Days 96 to 98): Smell, Swallowing, and First Expressions
The parts of the nose and brain that will one day sense smell keep developing, and your baby swallows small amounts of fluid. On day 83 the outer genitals are becoming clearer, and your baby may squint, frown, or move the mouth in small expressions. By day 84 your baby is almost 3 1/2 inches long from crown to rump and weighs about 1 1/2 ounces.

👅 Taste Buds Form
Your baby's tongue is covered with tiny bumps, and inside them, taste buds are forming. Taste buds sense sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and savory. By birth, a baby has more taste buds than an adult, spread over the tongue, the roof of the mouth, and the throat.
Taste buds forming is not the same as tasting. Over the coming weeks and months, the connections between the taste buds and the brain will grow. Later in pregnancy, your baby will swallow fluid that carries traces of flavors from the food you eat.

🌊 Flavors in the Water World
In one study, mothers who drank carrot juice often in late pregnancy had babies who later seemed to accept carrot-flavored cereal more readily than babies whose mothers did not. Other studies suggest that some flavors from a mother's food reach the fluid around the baby.
This does not mean you need special foods. It means that a varied, healthy plate in pregnancy may be one of the first ways your baby meets the tastes of your family's table. A colorful plate is good for you and may be good practice for your baby.

👃 Smell Is Being Prepared
The nose is not only for breathing. High inside it, special cells will one day sense smell and send signals to the brain. Those cells and their paths to the brain are developing now.
After birth, smell helps a newborn find the breast and recognize Mom. Studies show newborns are drawn to the smell of their own mother. God is preparing that bond now, long before the first meeting.
✝️ Paul wrote that believers are the pleasing aroma of Christ to God (2 Corinthians 2:15, CPDV).
🎂 Born January 22, 1931: Sam Cooke. Born in Clarksdale, Mississippi, he began in gospel and later sang "A Change Is Gonna Come." His voice became a sweet aroma that still lingers.
The first smells your baby knows will be the smells of home. Let your home carry the fragrance of love.

🍯 Taste and See
✝️ The psalmist invites us to taste and see that the Lord is good, and says that the one who hopes in Him is blessed (Psalm 34:8, CPDV).
🎂 Born November 11, 1960: Stanley Tucci. Known for his film roles and his love of Italian food, he hosted a TV series tasting his way through Italy. Taste and see that the Lord is good.
Faith is not only something we think about. It is something we experience.
This week, as God builds your baby's sense of taste, thank Him for every good thing you have tasted of His goodness. Write three of them in your journal. One day you will teach your child to taste and see the same goodness.

🩸 New Blood from the Spleen
In the early weeks, your baby's blood came from the yolk sac, and then from the liver. This week the spleen joins in, making red blood cells to carry oxygen to every growing part. Later in pregnancy the bone marrow will take over most of this work.
God moves the work of making blood from place to place as your baby grows. The body never runs short of what it needs.

🙆 A Neck and an Upright Head
For weeks, your baby's head has been bent forward over the chest. This week the neck lengthens and becomes more defined, and the head sits more upright. On an ultrasound, your baby looks more and more like a newborn. The arms are now long enough to match the size of the body, while the legs will catch up over the coming weeks.

🎀 Boy or Girl: Becoming Clearer
Your baby's sex was settled at conception, and the outer genitals have been developing over the last few weeks. This week they are becoming clearer, though they are not always easy to see on an ultrasound yet.
Most families who want to know learn on the detailed ultrasound around Week 18 to 22, or from a blood screening test done earlier. Some choose to wait for birth. Either way, God already knows, and your child is fully loved.

✨ Fine Hair Begins
Around this time, a very soft, fine hair called lanugo may begin to grow on your baby's skin. It will cover much of the body in the coming months and help hold the protective coating that forms later.
Most of the lanugo falls away before birth. Babies born early may still have some on their shoulders and back. It is a temporary covering, a gentle part of God's design for life in the water world.

🦋 The Thyroid at Work
Your baby's thyroid gland, in the front of the neck, is beginning to make its own hormones. Thyroid hormones help guide growth and brain development. Until your baby's thyroid is fully working, your thyroid hormones help too.
Iodine helps both thyroids do their work. Look for about 150 micrograms of iodine in your prenatal vitamin, as many experts advise. If you have a thyroid condition, your doctor will check your levels during pregnancy.

🌱 The Placenta Grows
The placenta keeps growing to match your baby's needs. It is now fully in charge of passing oxygen and nourishment to your baby and carrying waste away, and it makes the hormones that keep the pregnancy going.
At birth it will weigh about a pound. It is the first shared table between Mom and baby, set by God, and it serves faithfully for the whole pregnancy.

😊 Small Expressions
Around this time, your baby may begin to squint, frown, and move the mouth in small expressions. These are reflex movements as the muscles of the face grow and connect with the brain.
One day these same muscles will form your baby's first smile at you. God is building the face of joy.

📏 How Big Is Your Baby?
By the end of Week 14 your baby is almost 3 1/2 inches long from crown to rump, about the size of a peach, and weighs about 1 1/2 ounces. Your baby is growing faster now than at almost any other time in pregnancy.
✝️ "For who has despised the little days?" (Zechariah 4:10, CPDV).
🎂 Born January 10, 1949: George Foreman. He won Olympic gold in 1968, became the oldest heavyweight champion at 45, and sold millions of Foreman grills. Never despise the little days.

🎉 Welcome to the Second Trimester
From now through the end of Week 27 is the second trimester. For many mothers this is the most comfortable stretch. Nausea often fades, energy returns, and the bump begins to show.
In the coming weeks, you will likely feel your baby move for the first time, have a detailed anatomy ultrasound, and test for gestational diabetes. It is also a good time to prepare the home, take classes, and plan for the weeks after birth.

🎶 Why Singing, Not Talking? Week 14
Your baby's senses are developing one by one, and hearing comes later. Talking does not reach your baby yet, and understanding speech is a gift for after birth. God gave the waiting season a language, God's Unlimited Phonograms (phonic songs), passed spirit to spirit. As the senses wake one by one, your baby music becomes their first kids music.
Melody, rhythm, and pitch lead the way, and words follow. Lullabies and nursery rhymes travel down the family line for this very reason. Each song now builds a habit and a home that hearing will find ready.

🎧 Why Your Voice: The Headphone Method
No phone on the bump, please. Wear headphones and sing; the only voice in the room should be yours. Brothers, sisters, grandparents, and Dad can all sing like this.
Once hearing works, the steady sounds of Mom's body, and her voice riding on top of them, will fill your baby's world. Singing daily makes your voice the sound your baby will call home.

🔊 Sound Before Birth: What Science Shows
Babies learn the flavors of home before birth too. In a 2001 study, mothers who drank carrot juice in late pregnancy had babies who later enjoyed carrot-flavored cereal more than other babies did.
That flavor learning came in the last trimester, not in Week 14, and hearing will follow the same pattern of learning what is familiar. This baby music is a spiritual and family practice, not a medical treatment.

🥗 Eating for the Second Trimester
From now on, many women need only about one extra healthy snack a day. Your doctor can tell you what weight gain is right for you based on your weight before pregnancy.
Build each plate with vegetables and fruit, add protein such as eggs cooked until firm, beans, lean meat, or low-mercury fish, choose whole grains, and include milk or other calcium-rich foods. Eat a rainbow of colors. Your baby may be getting an early introduction to your family's table.

🐟 Smart Choices About Fish
Fish gives your baby omega-3 fats, especially DHA, that help build the brain and eyes. Many experts advise two or three servings a week of fish low in mercury, such as salmon, sardines, shrimp, cod, tilapia, pollock, and canned light tuna.
Skip shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish, bigeye tuna, marlin, and orange roughy, which are high in mercury. Cook fish until it flakes, and skip raw fish such as sushi and refrigerated smoked fish unless it is cooked.

💧 Water, Water, Water
Your body needs more water in pregnancy to make extra blood, keep the fluid around your baby fresh, and help prevent constipation and bladder infections. Many women need about 8 to 12 cups of fluid a day, more in hot weather or when exercising.
Keep a water bottle with you and sip through the day. If your urine is light in color, you are drinking enough.

🏡 Body: Caring for the Home This Week
Your baby's taste buds are forming, and flavors from your meals will later reach the water world, so eat a colorful plate. Keep your folic acid going every day, with greens, beans, citrus, firm eggs, whole grains, dairy, and low-mercury fish.
Even small amounts of alcohol are not known to be safe. A smoke-free car and a smoke-free home are gifts to your baby. Keep baths warm, not hot, and skip hot tubs and saunas. Let caffeine stay below the 200 mg mark. Check that milk and soft cheese are pasteurized, and heat deli meats before eating.
Even vitamins and herbal teas deserve a quick check with your doctor or pharmacist. Keep moving with gentle walks. I offer companionship and good information, not medical care, so let your midwife or doctor guide your health choices.

🧴 Skin Changes in the Second Trimester
Some women notice a dark line down the middle of the belly, darker nipples, or dark patches on the face. These changes are caused by hormones and usually fade after birth. Sunscreen and a hat outdoors can help keep facial patches from getting darker.
As your belly grows, stretch marks may appear on the belly, breasts, hips, or thighs. Lotions can ease dryness and itching, but no cream is proven to prevent stretch marks. They often fade to silver lines after birth. Call your doctor for severe itching, especially on the palms and soles.

🛏️ Sleep in the Second Trimester
Many women sleep better in the second trimester than in the first. Use this season to build good sleep habits: a regular bedtime, a cool dark room, no screens for an hour before bed, and ten quiet minutes in the listening corner to wind down.
Begin practicing sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees. It will help your back now and be ready when your bump is bigger.

🚶‍♀️ Moving With Your Growing Body
As your bump grows, your balance shifts. Wear supportive shoes, take stairs slowly, and hold the rail. Avoid ladders and step stools. Gentle exercise such as walking, swimming, and prenatal yoga keeps your muscles strong for the months ahead.
Stand up slowly from lying down by rolling to your side first and pushing up with your arms. This protects your back and belly muscles.

🦷 Dental Checkup
If you have not seen your dentist yet in this pregnancy, the second trimester is a good time to go. Mention the pregnancy when you book. Cleanings, fillings, and needed treatment are generally safe. Healthy gums are part of a healthy pregnancy.

👨‍🍳 For Dad: Cooking for Two
Dad, as her appetite returns, help her eat well. Learn to cook two or three simple, healthy meals, keep fruit and healthy snacks in the house, and share the shopping. Eat well together. Your baby's first introduction to your family's table is happening through her plate.
Keep praying with her and singing with her. Hand on her belly, pray, then hum this week's song together. Every sense God is forming will one day recognize home.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings
Grandparents can share a favorite family recipe and the story behind it. Big brothers and sisters can help plan a colorful meal for Mom: a red food, an orange food, a green food. Sing the weekly song together around the table.

🌸 Smell and Memory
Smell is closely tied to memory. A whiff of bread baking or a grandmother's perfume can bring back a whole childhood. After birth, your baby will learn the smells of home quickly: Mom's skin, Dad's shirt, the kitchen, the quilt.
Think about the smells you want your child to remember: clean laundry, a favorite meal, flowers from the garden. The smells of a peaceful, loving home become part of a child's sense of safety.

😊 The Joy of the Lord
When the people of Israel heard God's Word read again after a long time away, they wept.
✝️ Nehemiah told them not to grieve, but to eat and drink and share, because the joy of the Lord was their strength (Nehemiah 8:10, CPDV).
🎂 Born August 27, 1908: Lyndon B. Johnson. A former Texas schoolteacher, he signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and created Medicare. He liked to host big barbecues at his Texas ranch.
For many women, the second trimester brings a season of more energy and joy. Receive it as a gift. Let it give you strength for the work ahead, and share the joy with others.

💛 Teaching a Thankful Heart
✝️ Moses told the people that when they had eaten and were satisfied, they should bless the Lord for the good land He had given them (Deuteronomy 8:10, CPDV).
🎂 Born June 7, 1917: Dean Martin. From Steubenville, Ohio, he sang "That's Amore," a playful love song packed with Italian food. When you have eaten and are satisfied, bless the Lord.
Thankfulness after a meal is an old and holy habit.
Begin now: thank God after you eat, not only before. One day your child will hear you, and the habit of a thankful heart will be passed on through the most ordinary moments of the day.

🍽️ A Table Set by God
✝️ "He has led me out to the water of refreshment" (Psalm 23:2, CPDV).
🎂 Born June 11, 1933: Gene Wilder. He played Willy Wonka in the 1971 film, a story full of tastes and sweets. Your baby's taste buds are forming this week.
✝️ The same psalm says God prepares a table before us (Psalm 23:5, CPDV).
🎂 Born August 21, 1936: Wilt Chamberlain. He scored 100 points in a single NBA game in 1962, a record that still stands. God prepares a table before us, with more than enough.
God is a host who feeds His people well.
This week God is preparing your child to taste. You are preparing a table too: meals, prayers, and songs. Make your table a place of thanks. Pray before you eat, and let the weekly song be part of your mealtime.

🎵 One Song, Three Ways: Week 14
Each GUP song is learned three ways, and this week is no different. Preschool wisdom says: never teach the important thing only once. Hear it three ways and it will stay with you.

✍️ Hear It, Hum It, Write It
In the morning, hear it: a single listen in a quiet room. Thank God for the senses He is building in your child. At noon, hum it: hum together with the baby music in your headphones. Hum it before a meal, as a song of thanks. In the evening, write it: sit with your journal and listen. Catch each phonogram (phonic song) on paper, "ma," "loo," "ah," and keep the best for your First Sounds list.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-14 Pages
Write how the second trimester feels so far: your energy, your appetite, and your bump. Write three times you have tasted God's goodness, and a family recipe you hope your child will love.
Write this week's phonograms (phonic songs) and any picture or color the song stirred. Record fresh First Sounds, a prayer for your baby's senses, and a moment the family sang together.
✝️ "Write the vision and explain it on tablets" (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV).
🎂 Born April 13, 1922: Julius Nyerere. Known as Mwalimu, which means teacher, he led Tanganyika to independence and became Tanzania's first president. He wrote the vision for a nation.
That journal is becoming a family treasury of phonograms (phonic songs). These written sounds are seeds for the days ahead.

🙏 A Prayer for Week 14
"Father God, thank You for bringing us into the second trimester. Thank You for the taste buds, the senses, and the new blood You are making in our child. Let every sense You build one day lead our child to taste and see that You are good.
Make our table a place of thanks and our home a place of love. When hearing wakes, let our lullabies be the first thing our baby hears. In Jesus' name, amen."

💬 Questions Parents Ask

❓ Can my baby taste what I eat now?
Not yet. The taste buds are forming, and the connections to the brain are still growing. Later in pregnancy, traces of flavors from your food reach the fluid your baby swallows.

❓ Should I eat special foods to shape my baby's taste?
No special diet is needed. A varied, healthy plate is good for you and may introduce your baby to the flavors of your family's meals.

❓ When will I feel the baby move?
First movements are usually felt from Week 16 to Week 22, sometimes sooner if you have been pregnant before. The first movements are light flutters that are easy to miss, so be patient.

❓ Is it normal to be hungry all the time?
Many women feel hungrier in the second trimester. Choose healthy snacks, eat regular meals, and ask your doctor what amount of weight gain is right for you.

❓ Can I eat spicy food?
Yes, if it agrees with you. Spicy food is safe in pregnancy, though it may bring on heartburn. Later in pregnancy, some of those flavors may even reach the fluid your baby swallows.

❓ Why does my belly itch?
Stretching skin can feel itchy. Lotion and loose cotton clothes help. Severe itching, especially on the palms and soles, needs a call to your doctor.

❓ When do I call my doctor right away?
Call your doctor without delay for heavy bleeding, severe belly pain, fainting, a fever, a severe headache, leaking fluid, or severe itching, especially on your hands and feet.

✅ Your Week-14 Checklist: Body and Home
Each day I took my 400 micrograms of folic acid. I am eating a colorful plate. I know what my second-trimester visits will look like. I took nothing new without asking. I walked most days.

✅ Your Week-14 Checklist: Song and Prayer
Every day held all three: hearing, humming, writing. I added new sounds to First Sounds. I thanked God for my baby's senses. Someone I love hummed along.

🕊️ A Closing Blessing
✝️ "May the Lord bless you and keep you. May the Lord reveal his face to you and take pity on you. May the Lord turn his countenance toward you and grant peace to you" (Numbers 6:24-26, CPDV).
🎂 Born May 13, 1941: Ritchie Valens. He turned the Mexican folk song "La Bamba" into a rock hit before he died at 17. A short life can still bless millions.
May the God who is building your child's senses fill your home with good things, and may your song, the first kids music they know, be waiting when your child first hears.

D.C. police have identified human remains discovered behind a building along Georgia Avenue as Jahari Garrett, 25, of Northwest Washington. His death has officially been classified as a homicide.

▪️ DISCOVERY: Officers found the skeletal remains on May 15, 2026, behind the 2900 block of Georgia Avenue NW.

▪️ ADVANCED DECOMPOSITION: Investigators recovered remains that were already severely decomposed.

▪️ HOMICIDE RULING: The D.C. medical examiner classified Garrett’s death as homicide, although the exact cause remains undetermined.

▪️ INVESTIGATION ONGOING: Police have not publicly identified a suspect or announced an arrest.

▪️ $25,000 REWARD: Authorities are offering up to $25,000 for information leading to an arrest and conviction.

Five months after the discovery, a young man’s death remains unsolved. Investigators are asking the public to help identify whoever is responsible.

Anyone with information should call 202-727-9099 or text 50411.

text:
City Attorney Erika Evans is reinstituting Community Court, and giving people charged with non-violent misdemeanors 90 days to better themselves through "drug treatment, job support, health benefits, and peer services."

But Gee Scott brings up a great point:
Why does our city focus so heavily on coddling criminals, while allowing struggling, but otherwise law abiding citizens to fall through the cracks? A perfect example of this is parking enforcement.
Raise your hand if you've gotten a parking ticket in Seattle 
✋(Probably most of you who own a car are raising your hand right now, like I am)

But if you park your rundown RV at Woodland Park, smoking fentanyl and meth, dealing drugs, engaging in prostitution, and being a nuisance.....
The city will ask you nicely to move and offer you all sorts of assistance, with no obligation to accept it. And  the odds of you being charged with a crime for any of this is laughable under the current enforcement rules.

It is a fairness issue, and law abiding Seattleites keep getting the short end of the stick. City Attorney Evans is not necessarily wrong for restarting Community Court; but Seattle's track record on holding criminals accountable is so bad, we wonder if this is another attempt to circumvent consequences for people who need them.

I had to run this past @grok for the  full breakdown on Americans killed, injured or imprisoned by Israel and what how the governments have responded.  

 **As of October 16, 2026, the documented figures for Americans (mostly Palestinian-Americans or dual citizens) killed, injured, or detained in the West Bank context are as follows.** Precise real-time totals are incomplete because many cases involve dual nationals, and official US or Israeli tallies do not always isolate citizenship. The bulk of incidents occur in the occupied West Bank rather than inside Israel proper.[](<https://t.co/SyM8yhlAyj>)

**Killed**: At least nine American citizens have been killed by Israeli settlers or security forces in the West Bank since January 2022. Congressional resolutions and lawmaker letters list: Omar Assad, Shireen Abu Akleh, Tawfic Abdel Jabbar, Mohammad Khdour, Ayşenur Ezgi Eygi, Amer Rabee, Sayfollah Kamel Musallet, Khamis Ayyad, and Nasrallah Abu Siyam. No one has faced criminal conviction in these cases, according to US senators and advocacy groups. Some earlier cases (pre-2022) exist but are outside this recent count.[](<https://t.co/4iR7sLFFw5>)

**Injured**: Heidi Levine (Washington Post photojournalist, American) was severely beaten on October 16, 2026, by masked settlers during an olive-harvest attack near Abu Falah/Ramallah. She sustained lacerations, a broken rib, a deep hand wound, and other injuries; she was hospitalized and described being kicked for roughly 10 minutes while wearing a clearly marked PRESS vest. Other Palestinian-Americans were injured in the same wave of harvest-season attacks (e.g., in Turmus Aya). Dozens of Palestinians overall were reported injured that day; broader harvest-season and earlier settler attacks have injured additional dual nationals.[](<https://t.co/14WHlDmZJF>)

**Imprisoned/detained**: Several Palestinian-American minors and young adults have been held, frequently under administrative detention (without charge or trial). Recent examples include Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi (teen held ~4 months without charge as of early October 2026), Sama Safi, and Adam Karakrah. No single public aggregate of current US-citizen detainees is available; the overall Palestinian prisoner population in Israeli facilities is roughly 9,300, including thousands in administrative detention.[](<https://t.co/w2Kx5EGjkE>)

**US government reactions**: The State Department and US Embassy stated they were aware of the Levine reports, contacted the Washington Post to offer consular assistance, condemned “criminal violence by any party in the West Bank,” and supported investigations plus accountability. Statements generally avoided naming settlers as perpetrators in the immediate Levine case. Ambassador Mike Huckabee has previously (September 2026) called violent settler acts “terror,” visited affected Palestinian-American communities in places like Turmus Ayya, and urged “severe consequences.” As of the latest available reports, he had not issued a specific public statement on the October 16 Levine attack.[](<https://t.co/14WHlDmZJF>)

**Israeli government reactions**: The Prime Minister’s Office said the facts of the Levine incident remained “unclear and under investigation,” condemned violence against anyone in principle, but cited reports of roughly 200 “Arabs and far-left activists” confronting about 40 “Israeli youths,” mutual object-throwing, and disputed footage. It warned against using the events to “demonize” Jewish residents of the West Bank (Judea and Samaria). The IDF acknowledged a female journalist was injured in a “confrontation,” said it used riot-dispersal measures and fired toward a suspect carrying a sharp object, condemned violence against civilians, and stated details would be examined; police opened investigations. Critics noted the statements cast doubt on the video evidence of the beating.[](<https://t.co/GnmpBdherf>)

These patterns—high-profile injuries or deaths of Americans, limited accountability, and measured official statements—have been cited by US lawmakers in recent letters and failed resolutions seeking more reporting or sanctions. Data come primarily from congressional records, news reporting from multiple outlets, UN-related figures, and advocacy documentation as of mid-October 2026.

Watch for the G20 summit in Miami to see if this deal holds or collapses under geopolitical pressure.

text:
In recent months, I shared a few milestones from my life across my social media pages. They were small, but they represented critical milestones for me, and years of struggle, resilience, and continued effort.

The limited response on social media brought me back to something I have been reflecting on for some time, something that has been painful to acknowledge.

Leaving Facebook and Instagram last year revealed to me just how little support I already felt from many people I had considered part of my community, particularly throughout my educational journey and the years of struggle that followed.

It hurt tremendously, and I have to name that pain.

I recognized when I left those spaces that I may have lost even the limited conditional support I may have had. Because nobody from those spaces sought to connect with me in the other spaces I shared. Nobody subscribed for free on my YouTube or Substack. 

Not a single person reached out afterwards to check in and see if I was okay, knowing what I was struggling with. That made me realize that I was actually right about my inferences. 

I don't know many other women in my circles who have demonstrated the level of resilience that I have through tremendous personal struggle, and documented about it openly. 

If I encountered someone with a journey like mine, who had documented it over the years, I would be inspired by her. It would be an immediate natural impulse.

Instead... sometimes I feel I have been surrounded by people who seemed to resent my hard work, courage, and resilience rather than find inspiration in them.

Sharing some milestones recently brought those feelings back.

Even the smallest achievements can pass without acknowledgment from people whose own milestones you have celebrated for years. Not even professional spaces like LinkedIn are immune to this unevenness.

Support and recognition are not distributed equally, and this remains a largely unspoken phenomenon, perhaps because people are reluctant to admit that these things do actually matter to them.

I am honest about it, even as I continue to reflect and improve the way I perceive the world. 

But when you watch others repeatedly receive significant encouragement and recognition for an incredible accomplishment, while your own comparable achievements remain largely invisible, it can be difficult. Even when you are sincerely, genuinely happy for that person.

This is not simply about comparing ourselves to others online. I have worked really hard not to fall in the comparison trap.

But I have learned that support can be remarkably selective. And so can empathy and solidarity, particularly when differences in religious beliefs, political opinions, or personal circumstances enter the picture.

Such a pity.

I find it tragic, in the context of my own story, that relationships I once believed were grounded in mutual respect, support, and camaraderie have sometimes felt more like spaces of competition, jealousy, comparison, or quiet indifference. It has been so heartbreaking and difficult to navigate this. 

Perhaps I surrounded myself with the wrong people. Because when you see others experience things differently, you just wonder, why can't you be afforded that same type of love, support, and belonging. 

Or perhaps I placed too much faith in relationships that were never as reciprocal as I believed them to be.

As Oprah Winfrey reminds us, you have to believe people when they show you who they are. 

Living in Washington, DC, where professional competition and networking seem to dominate social relationships, has only made these realizations more difficult.

Admittedly, after I graduated from my doctorate, I used to anxiously anticipate the moment when I, too, would be able to share a significant update about the next chapter of my life after earning my PhD.

I watched others celebrate their appointments, promotions, and achievements. And I was genuinely happy for them. I cheered them on, believing that someday I, too, would have the opportunity to share that kind of news, especially as someone who had documented her entire educational journey online.

But years passed. 

Communities drifted apart. Relationships changed. And the longer my own struggle continued, the more I began to recognize the difference between people who celebrate your success and those who remain present while you are still fighting to reach it.

Sometimes, people may be willing to show up when something good finally happens in your life, but disappear entirely during the years when you're struggling, when you need encouragement the most.

I cannot adequately describe the pain of that realization, particularly as my professional struggles coincided with my advocacy for Palestine and the escalated genocide.

And sometimes, it has felt as though certain people took advantage of my vulnerability during this period, withholding care and support at a time when they knew I was struggling to keep moving forward in my academic journey.

Why is it so difficult for people to believe that such dynamics exist?

There are genuinely competitive people who do not have your best interests at heart. People who may never support or amplify your voice, precisely because they recognize your potential and perceive it as a threat, instead of an opportunity to collaborate.

There were moments when I felt that I was losing not only professional opportunities, but also the sense of belonging and support I had spent years trying to cultivate.

Perhaps someday I will find a more dignified way to describe this trying period of my life, after greater reflection.

But I also believe there is a reason these struggles have unfolded at this particular time.

As Muslims, we believe that Allah's plan is perfect, even when we cannot understand the wisdom behind it. Even when the experience feels brutal while we are living through it.

I have wondered why my professional and personal difficulties coincided so closely with the escalated genocide in Palestine... And why this particular period has demanded so much of my patience, faith, and resilience, at the same time, as I struggle to begin the next chapter of my life.

I do not know the answer, but I have a feeling that perhaps there is some sort of  preparation here for something even more difficult that may emerge in the future.

The blood, sweat, and tears of continuing my academics at this moment, during wars and genocide, have been far more painful than the blood, sweat, and tears of finishing my dissertation during the Pandemic. And at that time, I didn't think anything could be more difficult than that.

Now, there are days when I find myself longing for those years, rather than what I am enduring today. And I know the reasons why, both tangible and intangible. 

But I have to believe that there is wisdom in what Allah has decreed, and that our continued efforts, our patience, and our moral commitments, pursued with sincerity and integrity, are never without purpose.

Perhaps part of this experience is learning to distinguish between people whose presence in our lives is genuine and those whose support entirely depends on our circumstances, and whether we are able to overcome them.

It feels so cruel. This inconvenient truth. 

We do have to learn to forgive them, but forgiveness does not mean that we must continue allowing them to have VIP access in our lives.

Perhaps this is also an important lesson for me... 

No matter how much of an open book I have been, sharing my life on the internet, I no longer need to rush to share every small milestone publicly, hoping that the people I once considered my community will finally recognize what it took to get there.

It will still take some work to fully implement this in my life, because it requires changes in habitualized cognitive patterns and other bad habits. Change is supposed to be painful. 

Perhaps if there is any acknowledgment, it would not change very much, because I have continued making progress without their support during this brutal chapter. 

I no longer need their approval, validation, or recognition as proof of my perseverance.

I can celebrate and honor my achievements with gratitude to Allah, and with those who truly, genuinely wish me well.

I can continue pursuing the life and academic career I have worked so hard for, without allowing the silence of others to determine the value and worth of my efforts.

And I can remain hopeful that there are still people and communities I have yet to meet around the world who will appreciate what I have to offer, and recognize me not only when I succeed, but also while I am still trying...

For now, I have to focus on my work, protect my peace, and continue moving forward.

They say that the results of your work speak for themselves. But that is not always the case for everyone.

I have learned the hard way that no matter how many receipts I present to the world, support and care is not guaranteed. Even from loved ones and others who you always believed were standing in your corner.

And I have to learn to let that go. Let them go.

We can continue to share our milestones and accomplishments, but it is important to be prepared for the silence, and expect it. 

This may be an obvious lesson for many, but perhaps not for content creators and those of us who have spent years striving for love, encouragement, and support online, especially when faced with significant invisibility offline.

Alhamdulillah. Gratitude to Allah for every milestone, however small, and for the strength to keep going.

May He continue to remind us to purify our intentions, and may He bless us with the rizq and dignity we deserve as we continue our efforts toward success, prosperity, and happiness in this short life.

Ameen.

text:
Canada, I’m warning you now. 

When Carney signs that associate member deal with the EU, here’s what happens next, step by step. 

First, Trump doesn’t wait. 

He doesn’t send a diplomat. 

He doesn’t call a summit. 

He just acts. Energy gets hit first because that’s where Canada hurts most. Oil and gas flowing south slows down or stops. 

Not because Trump hates Canada, but because it’s the fastest way to make the point that choosing Europe has a price. 

Then it spreads. Autos, steel, aluminum, lumber, potash, beef. 

Every sector that depends on the American markte feels it within weeks, not years. 

The Canadian dollar drops. 

Interest rates climb. 

Provinces start cutting services because the money isn’t coming in like it used to. 

Europe won’t save us. They’ll issue statements. They’ll hold meetings. They’ll say they’re standing with Canada. 

But they can’t buy what we sell, they can’t ship it across the ocean at the same cost, and they can’t protect us if it turns into something worse than a trade fight. 

An associate membership  gives them influence over our rules without giving us anything that actually replaces what we’re losing. 

And here’s the part that should scare you most. 

This isn’t about one election or one prime minister. 

It’s about whether Canada stays a country that controls its own future or become a place where outside powers decide what we can and can’t do. 

The Monroe Doctrine was written 200 hundred years ago to keep Europe out. 

Trump is using it now to keep everyone out, including us if we don’t play along. 

You can call it fearmongering. You can call it politics. But the math doesn’t care what you call it. 

Three out of four things we sell go south. 

No deal with Brussels changes that. Not now, not in five years, not in twenty. 

So before you cheer for this and lift your elbows higher ask the people selling it one simple question. 

What exactly replaces the American market? 

Because if they can’t answer that, they’re not leading. They’re just hoping you won’t notice.

We seem to be on a suicide mission and signing that Associate Membership with the EU is just tightening the noose!

This isn’t a game!

Today I walked into a Catholic church in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, that could hold its own against the great basilicas of Rome.

And the story behind it is almost as magnificent as the church itself.
The Basilica of St. Josaphat was built by Polish Catholic immigrants, many of them working-class families who had come to America with little money but an extraordinary devotion to their faith.

By the 1890s, their parish had grown to more than 12,000 souls. Their first church had burned down. Their second was too small. So they decided to build something astonishing.

A church modeled after St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.

Their pastor, Father Wilhelm Grutza, learned that an enormous post office and customs building in Chicago was being demolished. He purchased it for $20,000, had it dismantled, and transported its materials to Milwaukee on FIVE HUNDRED railroad cars.

Stone by stone, these Catholic immigrants built their own little piece of Rome.

When the church was completed in 1901, its colossal dome was surpassed in size in America only by the dome of the U.S. Capitol.
But they weren't finished. After years of sacrifice and debt, the church's interior was transformed with magnificent Austrian stained glass, soaring columns, elaborate ornamentation, and breathtaking sacred paintings.

In 1929, Pope Pius XI elevated it to the dignity of a minor basilica—the first Polish-American church to receive that honor.

And the result?

One of the most magnificent Catholic churches in the United States. I have visited some of Europe's great churches, and this basilica genuinely rivals them in beauty and grandeur.
But what moved me most wasn't the dome or the artwork. It was the people who built it.

Ordinary Catholic families who understood something our age has largely forgotten: The house of God should lift man's eyes from earth to Heaven. They did built this for His glory.

And more than 125 years later, the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass is still offered beneath that magnificent dome.

Deo gratias.
St. Josaphat, pray for us. 🇵🇱

text:
'Swing' by: Vixyy Fox (a Halloween story)
Image by my daughter Laura Hollands

Many many people do not believe in ghosts. I do, because I have experienced them. My grandmother had the ‘touch’. I have the same, as does my daughter. Not all ghosts are bad and scary. What is scary is the unknown… and that’s what you’re dealing with; that infinite question of ‘what happens after we die’.

So you know, the first part of this story is true.

We had just moved into our new house around 1996. My daughter was still young then, perhaps around twelve years old. We began finding her sleeping on the floor of our bedroom, and asked her why. She said there was a ghost in her room. On a regular basis, she’d seen the silhouette of a man in the darkness, watching her. Being good parents, we told her it was a bad dream, and she should not be afraid. Eventually, she got used to him and told us his name was Fred. He lived in her closet.

Occasionally, while sitting in the family room, I would see a gray mist float past the doorway to the bedroom hallway. When that happened, I would say ‘Hello Fred.’ He never bothered us.

Years later, my mother-in-law was placed under hospice care, and her bed was in our living room. One day, I was sitting with her, and she began staring at the ceiling. Reaching out an arm in that direction, she said, “Fred.” In a moment of clarity, she looked at me, and asked, “Who’s Fred?”

I ended telling her the story. Perhaps she found comfort in this as she slipped away, perhaps not. All I can say for sure is that she didn’t join Fred in his haunting. When we moved, I offered to take Fred with us, but he chose to stay. He did bid me a farewell by knocking on the wall.

My daughter moved to England, and married. Her first house was next to an old American air force base from WWII. The runways were still there. I thought that was cool, and of course we went to visit. One night, while laying in bed, my wife and I thought the neighbors were having a party. We heard happy voices, all quite loud enough to just be annoying. We thought perhaps our daughter had her television on even though it was the middle of the night. That lasted until she popped her head in past our door and asked if we were making all the noise.

At this time of the year, meaning autumn, the world reflects upon death in the shadow of beautifully colored trees and a settling cold as if the season itself is reflecting upon the year’s own death, and the unknown of what will come in the new year. Mankind has long thought up ways of dealing with this. Holding hands with the same unknown, we tell scary stories, and invent things like leaving treats on the porch to appease the spirits, who, in turn, are glad to share with the children… and so, I will give you a story now.

The Swing

It was a simple child’s playground device, though there no longer was a playground, just as there was no longer a village. Almost everything had been destroyed by a fire set by the final occupants as they left, near sixty years before. Though the cemetery remained, the deserted community, considered cursed, was never rebuilt.

The spur line train tracks, old and forgotten, still remained. Occasionally day hikers might arrive to explore what once had been, but they never stayed long. All reported a great feeling of unease, dread, and nausea while there.

As the years passed, the forest semi-reclaimed what was left. Pretty much the entire village was overgrown with new growth trees and scrub brush… except for the playground, which remained clear as if the ground were poisoned. Anchored to the ground, mount poles jutting skyward from concrete feet, the swing set had stoutly resisted fading away. Rust covered the poles as if they’d contracted a disfiguring disease, and the one remaining cage swing looked more to be a child eating monster than a happy toy for children.

Mary Beth’s school class was having a picnic day in the country, hosted by an old farmer named Seth Michaels, who was church friends with their teacher, Miss Polly. The teacher’s class made this trip for two seasons of the year, and had been doing so for some time. The farmer was always happy for the visit, as was his wife, who prepared a nice lunch of hard boiled eggs, baloney sandwiches, and sweet tea for everyone.

In the Spring, when everyone was happy for warmer temperatures and the trees finally growing leaves again, they had the first picnic. Autumn, when all of the leaves were changing colors, and beginning to fall, they had the second.

This year, the Mr. Michaels offered to include a hayride out into the countryside around his farm. He proposed a trip to a place he called ‘Wentsville’, so the children could see for themselves, the village that was no longer there. The name was his own invention, as he knew the original name, and history, but refused to speak it. The folklore warnings he also knew, he chose not to speak of, because, ‘Why worry children with a repeat of scary stories?’

“There’s nothing there a’tall,” he told the class of thirteen children and their teacher, “Cept for an old cemetery, and what’s left of a few buildings. One of those buildings was the old school, and what’s left of its playground. I kinda thought you children would like to see what school was like sixty years ago, and no, your teacher was not there.”

His little speech, made in front of the tractor pulling their hay cart, was just after the wonderful lunch his wife had fixed. When one of the children asked him if the old tractor would be able to pull all of them, he happily patted its side and told them, “Of course it will. Nothing runs like a Deere.”

Everyone was happy, and climbed up on the hay bales, all placed strategically for sitting and such. More than a few of the children paired up, and more than a few hands were held. Mary Beth was no exception, finding herself sitting with a student she didn’t really recognize. For such a small class this was odd.

Introducing himself, the boy said his name was Dale. “I just arrived this morning, and the teacher gave me the desk at the back of the room,” he told her with a smile, and then offered to hold her hand.

Being a polite person, and taught the manners of hospitality, Mary Beth smiled back and made extra room for him on her hay bale, accepting his hand for holding. His touch was like ice. That was also the moment she first heard the sound… the soft metal on metal moaning noise a cage swing will make as it moves back and forth on its steel framework.

‘weeeee’ going back… ‘ahhhhhh’ going forward…

With a lurch, the big green tractor got them moving, and soon it, and the hay cart became shrouded by the shadows of the full autumn trees growing alongside the old railroad tracks. The sight was most beautiful.

In a few miles, they reached their destination, the tracks ending at a huge train bumper. Next to the track was what was left of a small depot. Mostly, what was there was a collapsed pile of wood.

Shutting his tractor off, the farmer blew his horn, stood in his seat, and addressed them as a group. “Welcome to Wentsville,” he yelled to them. “I will quickly point out some interesting things for you to visit, and then you may go and explore.” He then announced ‘Cemetery’, and pointed. ‘School’, and pointed. ‘Homes and such’, and here he circled his arm about encompassing the entire area. “Please be careful, and if there are any problems, sing out and I’ll come get you. We will be here for approximately two hours.”

Being that Mary Beth was already sitting with the new boy, she remained with him as, still holding her hand, he led her off at a run. “If we hurry, we can get to the playground before everyone else.”

“You’ve been here before?” she asked, doing her best to keep up.

He didn’t answer, but seemed to run even faster.

Breaking free of the forest slowly taking over the old village, they ran out into an open field. To the right of the field sat the remains of the old schoolhouse. The roof had collapsed into itself, and the walls that were left were gray-green and moldy. In the small bell tower remained the old  bell, now a solid green color covering what had once been new brass and shined once a week by the students.

In the middle of the field, equally decrepit yet still standing was a solitary swing set. The single remaining swing sat still and unmoving, though at first glance, Mary Beth thought she heard a soft moaning sound. It was like the old plaything was calling to her to use it just one last time.

“The village name was Everville,” Dale told her softly. “My father was the church leader, and founded the village, telling everyone ‘Like my name, now given to this village, the land it is built upon will forever be alive.’”

She was now afraid. “I don’t understand.” Looking at the boy who’d led her to this place, she found him to be totally pale. Though she’d never seen a dead person, she knew this was what they looked like.

He smiled at her. “Have you ever ridden a cage swing? It’s fun, and as you swing, it will sing to you. It’s a never ending song calling to you like that of the sirens who called to Ulysses. As you ride, your heart becomes more alive with the listening, and you find yourself flying ever higher and higher.”

“You rode the cage,” she whispered, beginning to understand.

“Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….” he sang to her, and she saw the swing begin to move, though there was no one sitting in it. “Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….”

“NO!” she protested, beginning to struggle.

His hand tightened around her wrist. “I insist,” he told her strongly, “In fact, my father is waiting.”

The school bell rang once, and Dale turned to stare at it. That had never happened before.

“Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….” the swing set sang, beginning to slowly move back and forth. “Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….” and Mary Beth felt it staring at her as if it had eyes.

“NO!” she yelled as loudly as she could, now struggling even harder. “HELP! HELP!”

The school bell rang twice, and Dale turned towards it. “Go away!” he yelled. “You’re dead, and all used up. This has nothing to do with you! YOU CANNOT INTERFERE!”

“Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….” the swing set sang, its voice sounding louder, as the boy pulled the struggling girl along, telling her how much fun it would be to ride the swing.

The school bell rang three times, and three young girls dressed in white nightgowns walked out of the foyer, followed by a forth, and a fifth, and a sixth. They were all holding hands, and in what seemed the blink of eye, placed themselves between the struggling pair, and the swing set.

“Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….” sang the swing set angrily, the cage now moving higher, and faster. Though it was just a swing, Mary Beth saw that it had a huge mouth, and a snake like tongue that writhed and twisted, dancing with the swing’s song of, “Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….”

“Go away!” Dale yelled at girls before him. “You’re dead! I know this because I fed you to the swing. It was payment to the devil against my father’s sins. This girl is the last payment, and then we’re all free! DO YOU NOT UNDERSTAND THAT?! WE WILL ALL BE FREE!”

His voice had a sound of desperation that hadn’t been there before.

Had Mary Beth not been screaming as hard as she could, she might have detected the sound of the farmer’s tractor as it slowly made its way through the trees. Though it was being pushed for all the speed it had, tractors were never meant to go fast… they were meant to be strong.

The school bell now rang in a continuous series of strikes, not fast, not slow, but strong and directed. Dale pressed his free hand over one ear, and screamed for the pain this was causing him. Releasing his intended prisoner, he covered his other ear, and sank to his knees.

Now free, Mary Beth did not run away. Though she was scared to the point of being terrified, she ran to the last of the girls in line and grabbed her arm, pulling all of them away from the huge gaping jaws of the swing. It’s snake like tongue spit forth and grabbed the first girl in line and a sudden tug of war began. The school house bell sounded out even louder than it had, each separate note seemingly now aimed at the swing like bullets from a pistol.

Dale, blinking, stared at his hands, and then screamed, ‘WHAT HAVE I DONE?!”

Jumping to his feet, he turned and ran towards the thing pulling at the girls, throwing himself at the snake, biting and clawing at it with every ounce of his remaining energy. At almost in the same moment the farmer’s tractor collided with the swing set from the side, ripping two of the stanchions out of the ground concrete and all. As the swing set screamed the tractor backed up and slammed into it a second time pulling a third leg out of the ground.

“Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh! Weeeeeeee… ahhhhhhhhhh….”  the child’s toy roared. The school bell also seemed to double its effort, now calling up an army of the wronged dead to bear witness to the destruction of the monster that had stolen their souls.

The tractor, its gearshift now forced into the lowest most powerful gear pushed into the remaining leg of the monster pushing it completely out of the ground. As it toppled over, a silence fell upon what had been the battleground of good and evil.

*****

Mary Beth woke on the back of the hay wagon. Her teacher sat beside her, sharing a mason jar of sweet tea with the farmer. Their soft words stopped when they saw she was awake.

“You gave us a bit of a scare,” her teacher told her, helping her to sit up. “How do you feel?”

“I’m fine,” she replied. “How is Dale, and the other girls?”

The farmer and teacher exchanged glances. “Best you call in the other children,” he told her. “I’ll take care of explaining things to her.”

When Miss Polly had left, Mr. Michaels helped Mary Beth down from the hay wagon and walked with her the short distance to the cemetery. “The reason this village was burned to the ground was the disappearance of the children. A good ten or twelve were never found.”

Coming into the small area of gravestones, he stopped before one of them, and motioned to it. “My sister was the first. This grave is empty, and only reflects the memory of who she was. My father, in a fit of absolute anger, shot and killed the church leader, when he ordered every one of the villagers to go home, and act as if nothing had happened, after the last little girl disappeared. In the man’s breast pocket, they found the child’s night hat. Leaving the body where it fell, they burned the church, then all the buildings, and left, forever.” He smiled at her, “You can see my family didn’t go that far away. My mother could not leave my sister, and so, twice a year we would come here to the cemetery and have a family picnic.”

“You saw her then… when we were fighting that thing?”

“The swing… yes, I did. It gave me the strength to do what needed to be done. She smiled at me, and I shall forever remember that.”

Mary Beth found his hand and squeezed it. “The front of your tractor is damaged.”

“It’s alright,” he told her softly, “I can fix that, and she’ll be as good as new.” He sighed, and then added, “Nothing runs like a Deere, and no swing set ever build, no matter how possessed, is a match for her.”
